Wider Sports News.title: Cancelled events, unpaid bills and uncertain vision: Will LIV Golf survive PIF’s exit?
Wider Sports News.summary: After the sudden withdrawal of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, LIV Golf has endured a tumultuous 2026. The once free-spending tour has cut prize purses, missed payments to contractors, and ended its season a week early. But with a new investor lined up, the LIV leadership remain confident of finding a new place in the sport. The post Cancelled events, unpaid bills and uncertain vision: Will LIV Golf survive PIF’s exit? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The tour that once trumpeted itself as ‘golf, but louder’ is making a quiet exit – for 2026, at least. The final season of LIV Golf in its original form is ending early at LIV Golf Indianapolis. A planned late August finale at the Team Championship in Michigan was called off, with steep budget cuts following the withdrawal of support from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

That decision was announced back in April, when all parties indicated that funding would continue through the 2026 campaign. The Michigan cancellation, however, is just one hint that life after PIF has already begun.

Wider Sports News.title: AD Ports Group hires HSBC to advise on L'imad takeover bid
Wider Sports News.summary: AD Ports Group hires HSBC to advise on L'imad takeover bid thenationalnews.com
Wider Sports News.body:
AD Ports Group, the integrated port, logistics chain and free zone operator, has hired HSBC to advise on a planned takeover bid by Abu Dhabi sovereign investment arm L’imad. The company’s board, which met through video conferencing, discussed the potential bid and “resolved to approve the appointment of HSBC Bank Middle East as the company’s financial advisers to oversee the transaction”, it said in a statement to Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, where its shares are traded.

The company offered no indication of a deadline for the transaction. L'imad this week announced it would bid to acquire 100 per cent of the AD Ports Group shares it does not already own, to expand its logistics portfolio.

Wider Sports News.title: Olympic champion Alistair Brownlee: ‘Triathlon incredibly healthy but probably needs consolidation’
Wider Sports News.summary: Two-time gold medal winner praises investment in the sport as World Triathlon moves to create centralised tour. The post Olympic champion Alistair Brownlee: ‘Triathlon incredibly healthy but probably needs consolidation’ appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Two-time Olympic triathlon champion Alistair Brownlee believes the sport is in an incredibly healthy position but thinks that greater consolidation may be needed. Triathlon was admitted to the Olympic Games in 2000, a development which catalysed participation levels and, more recently, has led to the creation of several major competitions and significant private investment.

These include SuperTri and the Professional Triathletes Organisation (PTO), which have joined the most established Ironman and World Triathlon circuits. However, apart from World Triathlon’s events, which include the Olympic competitions, all of these are privately run with varying levels of official recognition from the world governing body.

Wider Sports News.title: US$7bn team valuations, a streaming pilot and sponsor overhaul: The business of the 2026/27 Premier League season
Wider Sports News.summary: English soccer’s top flight remains in a commercial league of its own, but the 2026/27 Premier League season will herald a series of changes that could have a longer-term impact on its business. The post US$7bn team valuations, a streaming pilot and sponsor overhaul: The business of the 2026/27 Premier League season appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Barely a month after Spain lifted the Fifa World Cup at MetLife Stadium in New York, the Premier League returns this week after a summer that saw 182 of its players compete at soccer’s flagship international tournament.

Players have gradually been returning to their clubs for what represents the latest-ever start to a Premier League season, a delay largely driven by the expansion of the World Cup and the wider impact Fifa’s encroachment on the calendar has had on both scheduling and player welfare.

Wider Sports News.title: Why F1 believes ‘Americanisation’ is helping modernise the sport
Wider Sports News.summary: With three US races, quirky sponsorship designations, and a Brad Pitt-led Hollywood movie under its belt, the American influence on F1 is unquestionable. But Liam Parker argues the term ‘Americanisation’ is pejorative and should instead be viewed as the modernisation of the sport. The post Why F1 believes ‘Americanisation’ is helping modernise the sport appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The new cars are ruining the sport. The racing is too processional. The sport was better ‘back in my day’. These are just some of the accusations levelled at Formula One following the most recent alterations to the sport’s regulations.

True, they are the most significant modifications in a generation, but fan discontent following rule changes is nothing new. Whether it’s the start of the ground effect era in 2022, the introduction of hybrid engines in 2014, or the double diffuser drama of 2009, Formula One starting afresh and fan protests often go hand in hand – and that’s just this century.

Wider Sports News.body:
New York (July 22, 2026) – GSE Worldwide (GSE) today announced a strategic partnership with Extraordinary AI (EAI), an AI advisory firm specialising in enterprise AI adoption, to launch a firmwide initiative designed to embed artificial intelligence across the agency’s operations. The investment reflects GSE’s belief that AI will fundamentally reshape how sports and entertainment agencies operate by enhancing creativity, improving efficiency, and enabling teams to deliver smarter, more personalised solutions for clients. Through the partnership, GSE is proactively equipping its workforce with the knowledge, tools, and strategic framework needed to lead that transformation.

Through the initiative, employees from across GSE’s business will participate in a structured engagement that combines AI education, hands-on workshops and collaborative development sessions focused on identifying practical applications for artificial intelligence within the agency’s day-to-day operations. Rather than implementing off-the-shelf solutions, participants will develop AI-powered workflows and processes tailored specifically to GSE’s business and the needs of its clients.

Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has conceded that his famous 6/2 bench tactic “backfired” on his team against the All Blacks at Ellis Park, and it was an avoidable mistake.

South Africa, famous for their physical forward pack, opted to double down on that strength for game one of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series, stacking their bench with six forwards and just two backs as opposed to the traditional five forwards and three backs, which provides more even cover in the event of injury.

Rugby.title: Spencer to miss start of Bath's season after surgery
Rugby.summary: Bath captain Ben Spencer will miss the start of the 2026-27 season but Will Stuart and Jaco Coetzee among those returning.
Rugby.body:
Bath captain and England scrum-half Ben Spencer will miss the opening weeks of the 2026-27 Prem season after having surgery on a long-standing shoulder injury. The 34-year-old missed two games for Bath in April after he injured his shoulder; however, he returned to conclude the season and was part of England's squad this summer for the Nations Championship, coming on as a replacement during the win away in Argentina.

Bath said Spencer will return "later in the autumn". The club begins the 2026-27 season away at Harlequins on Friday, 25 September. Louis Hennessey, Tom de Glanville, Will Muir, Tom Dunn and Sam Underhill have all also undergone shoulder procedures this summer however will be available for the start of the campaign.

Rugby.title: Blow for Bath as Ben Spencer is ruled out for start of season
Rugby.summary: The scrum-half, who led Bath to the PREM title in 2025, had an operation this summer to resolve a longstanding issue, with the club confirming he will return "later in the autumn."
Rugby.body:
Bath captain Ben Spencer will miss the opening rounds of the 2026/27 PREM Rugby season as he continues to recover from shoulder surgery. The scrum-half, who led Bath to the PREM title in 2025, had an operation this summer to resolve a longstanding issue, with the club confirming he will return “later in the autumn.”

Presumably, this means Spencer will miss the first three league fixtures at least, Harlequins (away), Exeter (home) and Northampton (away). Spencer is just one of several Bath players battling to recover from shoulder injuries, but Louie Hennessey, Will Muir, Sam Underhill, Tom Dunn and Tom de Glanville are on schedule to be fit for the new season.

Rugby.summary: Louise McMillan turned down a contract from Scotland at the start of the year and has now retired from international rugby at the age of just 29.
Rugby.body:
Louise McMillan turned down a contract from Scotland at the start of the year and has now retired from international rugby at the age of just 29. The second row lost her Scotland contract in the summer of 2025 after first being awarded one in 2022. That meant she had to get a full-time job again, working in operations for an insurance company.

If she was going to be a full-time rugby player again she would have had to take a pay cut and make other sacrifices and at this point in her life, she felt it was something that didn’t feel right.

Rugby.title: Erasmus leaves door open for late changes with five Springbok injury updates
Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus may have named his matchday 23 to face the All Blacks in game two of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series, but he says there are a couple of changes that could yet be made.
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus may have named his matchday 23 to face the All Blacks in game two of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, but he says there are a couple of changes that could yet be made.

It remains unclear whether captain Siya Kolisi will be fit in time to play, and superstar winger Cheslin Kolbe is hanging under a similar injury cloud. While Kolisi’s name appeared on the team sheet, it was listed alongside Paul de Villiers, with a slash between them, signalling that the latter would step in should Kolisi not recover from his hamstring injury in time. Meanwhile, Kolbe’s name was left off the team sheet entirely, with Kurt-Lee Arendse named on the right wing.

Rugby.title: Edinburgh add ex-international to their new-look coaching team
Rugby.summary: Former Australia 7s player Michael Hodge has signed a two-year deal to become the capital club's skills and contact coach.
Rugby.body:
Former Australia 7s player Michael Hodge has signed a two-year deal to become Edinburgh’s new skills and contact coach. Hodge, 37, joins a coaching group spearheaded by head coach Sean Everitt, alongside Tim Sampson (attack), Brad Davis (defence) and Stevie Lawrie (forwards).

He arrives from the IRFU, where he served as Ireland Men’s U20 Assistant Coach, having previously held the role of National Elite Player Pathway and Men’s U18 Head Coach. “I’m incredibly proud to be joining Edinburgh Rugby. Moving over to Ireland has been a brilliant experience, both personally and professionally, and I’m grateful for the opportunities I had to continue developing as a coach. But this is a fantastic opportunity and one I couldn’t turn down,” said Hodge.

Rugby.title: 'On a beggar's ration, New Zealand gave Rassie Erasmus' Springboks a dig in the ribs'
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks' scrum stood up admirably as New Zealand reminded South Africa of the stark difference between winning possession and using it.
Rugby.body:
The most famous chapter in the six-part novella fought between ‘Sugar’ Ray Robinson and Jake La Motta was the epitaph in Chicago on 14th February 1951. By the 13th round the right arm of the Bronx Bull was hanging limply by his side and the Sugarman was slugging him to body and head at will. La Motta stayed on his feet, refusing to go down and taste canvas for the first time in his career, and the 1980 movie Raging Bull immortalizes the final moments in grainy back and white. A bloodied, exhausted Robert De Niro hangs on the top rope with one hand, while taunting Robinson to deliver more punishment with the other. Not for nothing has that fight passed into boxing lore as ‘The Saint Valentine’s Day Massacre’.

Over one month ago, this RugbyPass piece signalled the Greatest Rivalry series would be fought on a philosophical battleground in the no man’s land between ‘contest’ and ‘no-contest’, between winning the ball and using the ball. In recent times, progress in the game has been associated with the bulge in ball-in-play time, more phases and fewer set-pieces, and ever more try-scoring. The Nations Championship averaged over 37 minutes of ball-in-play time, nine tries and more than 200 total rucks per game.

Rugby.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said Handre Pollard has delivered for the Springboks "under extreme pressure" when explaining why he has opted to start the double World Cup-winning fly-half in the No.10 jersey for the second Test against the All Blacks in Cape Town on Saturday.
Rugby.body:

Having lost the first Test 33-16 at Ellis Park, the Springboks head into this match knowing a defeat at the DHL Stadium would render it impossible to win the four-match Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

Rugby.title: Boks drop Feinberg-Mngomezulu to bench for All Blacks rematch
Rugby.summary: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu pays for an indifferent showing in South Africa's series opener against New Zealand, as the fly-half drops to the Springbok bench.
Rugby.body:
Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has paid the price for an indifferent showing in South Africa's defeat by New Zealand, with the fly-half dropping to the bench for Saturday's rematch in Cape Town.

The All Blacks, revitalised under new coach Dave Rennie, ran out 33-16 winners in the series opener in Johannesburg. Feinberg-Mngomezulu was turned over five times in possession and occasionally exposed in defence, before he shifted to full-back for the Springboks in the second half of Saturday's first Test.

The 60-cap Bok, who started his career at the Lions and moved to Sale Sharks in 2017, has been in superb form for the Cheetahs, prompting Dobson to explore signing him on loan.

Rugby.title: Injuries take toll on Boks with 4 changes to XV as Erasmus makes peculiar Kolisi move
Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus has named his South Africa side to take on the All Blacks in the second Test of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series, with potentially four changes to the starting XV.
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus has named his South Africa side to take on the All Blacks in the second Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, with potentially four changes to the starting XV.

In what is a seldom-seen move, Erasmus has named captain Siya Kolisi to start, but has “bracketed Siya alongside Paul [de Villiers],” to give the coaching team more time to monitor the 35-year-old through training this week as he returns from a hamstring injury. This goes against Erasmus’ long-held mantra that you can only play at the weekend if you can train on Monday.

Rugby.title: Jason Ryan likens All Blacks' scrum battle to '12 rounds of boxing'
Rugby.summary: Ryan, speaking to Scotty & Izzy on Sport Nation NZ, Ryan described how he saw the scrum battle from up in the coaching box at Ellis Park.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Jason Ryan has likened the scrum battle against the Springboks to “12 rounds of boxing” after escaping Johannesburg with a Test victory. Their 17-point triumph over the back-to-back World Champions had everything, from scrum penalties to cynical yellow cards; the game ebbed and flowed, culminating in an All Blacks victory in front 60-thousand at Ellis Park.

Those scrum penalties, an area the Springboks dominated for large parts of the contest, turned the result in the All Blacks’ favour late on, with Dave Rennie’s bench adding much-needed stability at scrum time.

The Black and Ambers marked the occasion – the first same-sex blessing held at St Basil's Church in Bassaleg – with a post on social media. It was another step for a back-row forward who has been "out" with his team-mates since 2018.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga weighs in on the All Blacks' new attacking game plan
Rugby.summary: According to Mo'unga, it hasn't taken him long to adjust to the new game-plan, and in fact, it's something the 32-year-old is excited about.
Rugby.body:
56-Test All Blacks playmaker Richie Mo’unga is impressed with the “exciting” way Dave Rennie’s side are going about their business, after winning seven from seven in 2026. Even without featuring for the All Blacks under Rennie, the Canterbury first-five has gotten a feel for the optimism surrounding the camp on Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour of South Africa.

The last time Mo’unga pulled on the All Blacks jersey was in 2023 in France at the Rugby World Cup, a moment that will soon be in the rearview mirror. The All Blacks first-five will start in the playmaking roles alongside longtime international teammate Beauden Barrett to take on the Lions at Ellis Park on Wednesday.

Rugby.title: The Springboks' brawn was impressive, but the brains were sadly lacking
Rugby.summary: The brawn was impressive at Ellis Park, but the brains were sadly lacking and it was an incredibly untidy performance for a team that was so physically dominant.
Rugby.body:
Now that’s out of their system, you hope the All Blacks and Springboks might play some rugby. The brave team beat the dumb team at Ellis Park. You have to commend New Zealand for continuing to turn up defensively and celebrate the front row depth that enabled them to beat South Africa 33-16 in Johannesburg.

I knew Asafo Aumua could scrummage, but I feared George Bower lacked the grunt of Ethan de Groot. As it was, de Groot was the prop who had his backside handed to him by the Springboks and Bower who helped shore up a weakness that was going to cost the All Blacks this test.

Rugby.title: Grant Williams was targetted in defence by the All Blacks
Rugby.summary: New Zealand already had a recipe that worked, yet Erasmus and his team went again with Williams. For the second time, it backfired.
Rugby.body:
Springboks halfback Grant Williams was an unusual No.9 selection for South Africa. The main reason being that at Eden Park last year the All Blacks unsettled him, throwing South Africa off their game. New Zealand already had a recipe that worked, yet Erasmus and his team went again with Williams. For the second time, it backfired.

Every coach loves versatility. Williams can cover wing, which was needed in this game, but they forgot to keep the main thing the main thing. The No.9 has to be the best halfback first and foremost. If the No.9 is harassed and put under pressure, the entire cohesion of the backline or shape is out of sync.

Rugby.title: The three trouble positions which the Wallabies must resolve in Argentina
Rugby.summary: Los Pumas is the perfect litmus Test for the Wallabies, and has been so since Michael Cheika first coached the side in a Test in 2021.
Rugby.body:
Les Kiss has now named the second squad of his tenure as Wallabies head coach, reducing it from 36 to 34 players for the trip to Argentina. For the first time in 2026, no debutants have been selected in the squad, and this bodes well for consistency and for the wider group really cementing its identity.

The omission of giant lock Miles Amatosero was expected as he serves a three-match ban for his illegal hit on Japan’s captain Warner Dearns in Osaka. The unexpected omission is that of Queensland Reds’ fullback Jock Campbell, who played excellently in the Wallabies’ narrow defeat to Ireland in July.

Rugby.summary: "It's really special. It's been a long time, but I'm just really grateful to be back in this environment, thankful to Rens and the coaches for giving me this opportunity and also having trust that I can do a job."
Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga not the only new face in All Blacks team to play Lions
Rugby.summary: Patrick Tuipulotu will captain an overhauled All Blacks team to play the Lions in the final midweek game of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test series.
Rugby.body:
Patrick Tuipulotu will captain an overhauled All Blacks team to play the Lions in the final midweek game of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series. The headline selection, long expected since his highly anticipated return to camp, is Richie Mo’unga coming in at 10. It will be Mo’unga’s first appearance in a black jersey since the 2023 Rugby World Cup final. The playmaker will link up with Beauden Barrett, who starts at fullback, and will be backed up on the bench by Josh Jacomb.

Other new faces to the tour, Noah Hotham and Saula Ma’u, will get their first minutes in South Africa, the latter coming into the game as uncapped. Both Jamie Hannah and Ofa Tu’ungafasi are straight off the plane and onto the field after coming in as cover for Ethan de Groot and Josh Lord, who went down in Saturday’s dramatic win over the Springboks.

Rugby.summary: Jesse Kriel insists the Springboks remain firmly in the fight despite their heavy Ellis Park defeat to the All Blacks...
Rugby.body:
Jesse Kriel insists the Springboks remain firmly in the fight despite their heavy Ellis Park defeat to the All Blacks, with the South Africa captain viewing the remaining three Tests of the Greatest Rivalry series as knockout rugby.

The Boks now head to Cape Town needing three consecutive victories to claim the series, but Kriel said belief remains high within the camp. “Of course, I think anything is possible in rugby,” said Kriel when asked if South Africa could still win the series 3-1.

The Boks now head to Cape Town needing three consecutive victories to claim the series, but Kriel said belief remains high within the camp. “Of course, I think anything is possible in rugby,” said Kriel when asked if South Africa could still win the series 3-1.

Sweat is pouring off Alisha Joyce and Georgia Evans as they emerge exhausted from the spin bike chamber at Wales' training base. They collapse to the floor fighting for breath as head coach Sean Lynn gives them an encouraging tap on the back.

Next door in the gym Maisie Davies changes the playlist to "It's my birthday" while the forwards go about completing their sets in search of personal bests. And out on the artificial pitch, Ashley Beck is putting the backs through their paces, with uncapped Amy Williams catching the eye.

Rugby.title: All Blacks never-say-die grit pays as Rassie sinks his own ship
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks 33-16 win over the Springboks was a classic story of weathering the storm and winning the little moments that matter.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks‘ 33-16 win over the Springboks was a classic story of weathering the storm and winning the little moments that matter. Despite their ‘dominance’, the Springboks were repelled from entries into the 22 and left coming away with zero points on multiple occasions, with the All Blacks delivering on resilience and grit to give themselves a shot in the back end of the game.

A heroic save by Jordie Barrett forced a knock-on from Malcolm Marx when the hooker looked certain to score from a rolling maul. The midfielder’s never-say-die act is no fluke.

Rugby.title: 'Walking around': Rennie questions Springbok scrumming tactic after set piece struggle
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks scrum came under immense pressure all afternoon in Johannesburg with the visitors unable to stabilise the set piece until the reserve front rowers came on.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks scrum came under immense pressure all afternoon in Johannesburg with the visitors unable to stabilise the set piece until the reserve front rowers came on. The Springboks used their strength to their advantage, looking to shove the All Blacks off the ball at every opportunity. When halfback Cam Roigard couldn’t get the ball out quickly, the All Blacks were penalised on their own feed multiple times.

South Africa flexed their advantage at scrum time but a key reversal came when the home side doubled down on scrums after winning a penalty in front of the posts, turning down points to go again with the score at 19-16.

Rugby.title: 'It was the right call': Dave Rennie weighs in on Ardie Savea's tackle on Jasper Wiese
Rugby.summary: A dramatic turning point in the All Blacks 33-16 win over the Springboks came with the All Blacks looking to land the definitive blow with a 10-point lead.
Rugby.body:
A dramatic turning point in the All Blacks 33-16 win over the Springboks came with the All Blacks looking to land the definitive blow with a 10-point lead. A Quinn Tupaea 50-22 turned the screws and had the Boks pinned deep in their 22, but a loose ball turnover ended up in the hands of Jasper Wiese. The No.8 powered through the tackle of Ardie Savea, before the All Blacks captain pinched a breakdown steal two phases later to put New Zealand back on attack.

A grubber kick from Jordie Barrett pinned the Boks on the five, where a strong counter-ruck won back possession, before reserve flanker Marco van Staden played halfback Cam Roigard, coming from a side entry to disrupt play.

Rugby.summary: Both squad members will miss the Lions midweek fixture, and will be under a concussion protocol cloud ahead of the second Test in Cape Town.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have been forced to fly over two more squad reinforcements to South Africa, with 68-Test versatile prop Ofa Tu’ungafasi and Crusaders lock Jamie Hannah the chosen two.

Tu’ungafasi is yet to feature for Dave Rennie in 2026, while Hannah made his Test debut in Christchurch against France at One New Zealand Stadium. Rennie made the call after loosehead prop Ethan de Groot and lock Josh Lord clashed heads in the first Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry against South Africa.

Rugby.summary: Monaco Rugby Sevens Triumphs in Biarritz, Secures 2027 Supersevens Final Spot Nice-Matin
Rugby.body:
Monaco Rugby Sevens made the perfect start to its In Extenso Supersevens campaign in Biarritz, combining relentless defense with attacking flair to claim the opening tournament and book an early place in the 2027 grand final in Paris.

With the competition’s new format combining pool play and knockout matches, there is little room for error. That is especially true with only two qualifying tournaments, making the season opener in Biarritz a crucial opportunity for Monaco Rugby Sevens to get its In Extenso Supersevens campaign off to the best possible start.

Rugby.title: 'Nothing in that game': Rennie delivers blunt assessment after victory over Boks
Rugby.summary: "Ethan de Groot was crook overnight, and but yeah, look, we're really happy with with the effort up front, and scrum was really solid in that last 30."
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has provided his initial thoughts on his side’s important first Test victory over the Springboks at Ellis Park. The All Blacks, who trailed at half-time by one point, overcame the back-to-back World Cup winners in Johannesburg to take a 1-0 lead in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series.

Their 33-16, five-tries-to-one victory over the Springboks was built off an impressive second-half performance, despite trailing at halftime. Will Jordan’s late five-pointer sealed the deal for Rennie’s men, but the head coach was quick to cool the jets on the performance.

Rugby.body:

The South Africa coach was highly complimentary of his opponents when addressing reporters shortly after the full-time whistle, offering credit for their execution on both sides of the ball and ability to generate a period of game-changing momentum as the match ticked into its final quarter.

Rugby.title: The Springboks got drunk on their own hype
Rugby.summary: Wellington, 2025. New Zealand beaten by a record score. 43-10. Thirty-six unanswered points in the second half. A brace for Cheslin Kolbe. A masterclass from Damian Willemse. Six tries to one.
Rugby.body:
Wellington, 2025. New Zealand beaten by a record score. 43-10. Thirty-six unanswered points in the second half. A brace for Cheslin Kolbe. A masterclass from Damian Willemse. Six tries to one.

We heard about that game so often in the build-up to this Test that it began to feel like a reference point for the new Springboks. Proof that South Africa had evolved. That Tony Brown had added wit to the muscle. That the Boks could still bludgeon teams, but could now also manipulate space, shift the point of attack and unleash their backs before a defence had time to settle.

The four-Test series between the All Blacks and the Springboks has hit the ground running at Ellis Park, with Dave Rennie’s side overcoming the back-to-back World Cup winners, 33-16.

Rugby.body:
Springboks player ratings: South Africa started Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry in disastrous fashion, losing 33-16 to the All Blacks on Saturday at Ellis Park. The match was played with a level of physicality that, in truth, forced penalties from either side early on.

Rugby.summary: Even by Ellis Park standards, Saturday evening's Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test series opener was a raw and vicious encounter.
Rugby.body:
Even by Ellis Park standards, Saturday evening’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series opener was a raw and vicious encounter. Were it not for the feverish crowd, the sounds of bodies colliding would have been heard from the farthest reaches of the Eastern Cape.

The series opener lived up to the billing of ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’, delivering action on all fronts. The All Blacks were ahead by 10 points with 12 minutes remaining when South Africa sealed their fate with two yellow cards. One more try from the Kiwis was the cherry on top for Dave Rennie.

Rugby.summary: Prem Rugby side Leicester Tigers sign New Zealand-born Tonga international hooker Sam Moli.
Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers have signed Tonga international hooker Sam Moli. The New Zealand-born forward has joined after leaving Super Rugby side Moana Pasifika after they disbanded following financial issues earlier this year.

Moli, 27, made 47 appearances in four years with Moana Pasifika and has won 27 caps for Tonga since his debut in 2021. "Sam comes and adds some quality and depth to our hooking options," said Tigers head coach Geoff Parling.

Rugby.summary: HSBC SVNS Series star Maddison Levi didn’t want her Wallaroos debut to end, having come off the bench with 30 minutes left.
Rugby.body:
HSBC SVNS Series star Maddison Levi didn’t want her Wallaroos debut to end, having come off the bench with 30 minutes left in a 67-19 defeat to the Black Ferns. “I wanted to keep playing,” Levi said post-game, having made a noticeable impact in limited time out on the field.

Levi is the all-time leading try-scorer for the Australia Women’s Sevens side, went to the Olympic Games in Tokyo and Paris, was named the 2024 World Rugby Sevens Player of the Year, and has won multiple SVNS Series events.

Rugby.body:

Desiree Miller scored in the final play of the first half, but the New Zealanders would go on to add another 33 unanswered points to their tally in the second term. It was a masterclass from start to finish for the Black Ferns, who will soon jet off to South Africa.

Rugby.body:
Tasman Mako winger Kyren Taumoefolau has already scored 10 tries in the National Provincial Championship this season, backing up a historic five-try haul with another two in an emphatic 46-17 win over Southland.

Taumoefolau ran in a hat-trick against North Harbour in round one, before getting back on the scoresheet two weeks later. The 23-year-old Tongan international, who will become eligible to play for the All Blacks in October, scored five in a win over Counties Manukau.

Rugby.summary: Ardie Savea is back in the All Blacks camp and is "hungry to get going" after two weeks of rest, during which he watched his team begin the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour with three wins.
Rugby.body:
Ardie Savea is back in the All Blacks camp and is “hungry to get going” after two weeks of rest, during which he watched his team begin the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour with three wins.

The Kiwi captain said he hasn’t looked to assert himself on the team since joining them in Johannesburg, only looking to “add to the energy that’s already here”, happy with the momentum that’s been built in his absence.

Rugby.title: High court allows rugby brain injury case to go on
Rugby.summary: The cases of hundreds of players in rugby's multi-million-pound concussion legal battle allowed to continue after High Court ruling.
Rugby.body:
The cases of hundreds of players in rugby's multi-million-pound concussion legal battle have been allowed to continue by the High Court. A judge last month considered whether to throw out the claims due to failure to comply with an order to provide documents surrounding the neurological testing process.

Senior Master Jeremy David Cook has now allowed the legal battle, which has already stretched six years, to continue to trial after a change in lawyers representing more than 500 players from both rugby union and league.

Rugby.title: Wales great Jones returns to Ospreys as a director
Rugby.summary: Ospreys confirm former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones as a new member of their board before the 2026-27 season.
Rugby.body:
Ospreys have confirmed the return of former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones as a director. The 40-year-old has become a board member at the Swansea-based team with immediate effect.

Jones made his Ospreys debut in 2005, a year after he broke through with Swansea RFC, and helped the club to three titles and an Anglo-Welsh Cup triumph. The former lock is to return at a turbulent time amid their fight for survival under Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) plans to cut to three professional men's sides.

Rugby.title: Coach Stick: Why Paul de Villiers is 'the right person' to face All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Paul de Villiers will start for the Springboks in his first game against the All Blacks, stepping in for talismanic leader Siya Kolisi as the Springboks take a cautious approach to the captain's return from injury.
Rugby.body:
Paul de Villiers will start for the Springboks in his first game against the All Blacks, stepping in for talismanic leader Siya Kolisi as the Springboks take a cautious approach to the captain’s return from injury.

But De Villiers’ selection wasn’t entirely a health-based decision. Springboks coaches backed the 23-year-old’s form, allowing them to give Kolisi an extra week’s rest. De Villiers has started the Springboks’ season, his first with the team, as the starting openside flanker, and has retained that jersey in every Test since, except for South Africa’s most recent, a low-scoring win over Argentina.

Rugby.title: 'I absolutely loved it': How a 330km walk kept Rhona Lloyd on the pitch
Rugby.summary: Last year Rhona Lloyd was contemplating retiring following the Women's Rugby World Cup after falling out of love with the game.
Rugby.body:
Last year Rhona Lloyd was contemplating retiring following the Women’s Rugby World Cup after falling out of love with the game. The Scotland winger struggled after being left out of the GB sevens squad for the 2024 Paris Olympics and didn’t have time to process the omission as she went straight into that year’s WXV 2 in South Africa.

The 29-year-old needed some time away from the game before the Women’s Rugby World Cup and that came in the form of the Camino de Santiago 330km walk. “I was really not enjoying rugby and at a stage where I didn’t know if I wanted to keep playing after the World Cup,” Lloyd said.

Rugby.title: World Cup-winning duo headline 13 international re-signings at Exeter
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs have confirmed the re-signing of 13 internationals prior to the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby season.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs have confirmed the re-signing of 13 internationals prior to the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby season. This includes all five of their capped Red Roses, including Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 winners Maddie Feaunati and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, as well as Maisy Allen, Emily Robinson and Flo Robinson.

Club centurion Merry Elworthy, along with Taz Bricknell, Sofia Bekir Fuente, Lucy Nye and Sammy Wong have also signed on for more. Last season Exeter finished third in the PWR table and exited the play-offs with a defeat to eventual champions, Saracens.

Rugby.summary: Evie Gallagher was part of the Scotland squad that reached a record high of fifth in the World Rugby rankings two years ago.
Rugby.body:
Evie Gallagher was part of the Scotland squad that reached a record high of fifth in the World Rugby rankings two years ago and was also part of the squad that put in an excellent showing versus Wales a year ago at the Women’s Rugby World Cup in England.

And, after a frustrating one-win Guinness Women’s Six Nations campaign, the fit-again Bristol Bears No.8 believes the Scots can find that level again – and she says they will be playing “a completely different brand of rugby” during the upcoming WXV Global Series than what we saw earlier in the year.

Rugby.title: 'It's exciting': Fijiana XV squad named for WXV Global Series Challenger
Rugby.summary: New Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker has named his WXV Global Series Challenger squad that will travel to Hong Kong China next month.
Rugby.body:
New Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker has named his WXV Global Series Challenger squad that will travel to Hong Kong China next month. Installed as head coach shortly before Fiji’s two-Test encounter with the Springbok Women, Walker has opted for consistency heading into fixtures with Spain, Hong Kong China and the Netherlands at Kai Tak Sports Ground.

Scrum-half, Kolora Lomani, continues to captain the side, who are without Adi Salaseini Railumu, Sulita Waisega and Loraini Senivutu after they were ruled out with injury. Breakout star of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, Manuqalo Komaitai, will join up with the squad in Japan, ahead of the team’s clash with the Sakura Fifteen in Fukuoka.

Rugby.title: The domestic league supplying 13 of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test players
Rugby.summary: Japan Rugby League One’s influence on the international game will be in plain sight when Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry gets underway at Ellis Park on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Japan Rugby League One’s influence on the international game will be in plain sight when Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry gets underway at Ellis Park on Saturday. When Springbok and Toyota Verblitz back-rower Pieter-Steph du Toit and Kobelco Kobe Steelers No.8 Ardie Savea lead their sides out in Johannesburg, they will be among 13 players with League One links selected across the two matchday squads.

The figure certainly speaks to how far the competition has come since its launch five years ago. A quarter of the players involved in the opening Test come from Japan’s domestic league, with another three members of the coaching teams also bringing League One connections.

Rugby.title: Rassie's tribute to Damian de Allende ahead of 100th Sprinboks Test
Rugby.summary: Damian de Allende's name will enter the hallowed halls of Springboks history once again this weekend, when the 34-year-old runs out for his 100th Test match for the team.
Rugby.body:
Damian de Allende’s name will enter the hallowed halls of Springboks history once again this weekend, when the 34-year-old runs out for his 100th Test match for the team. The bruising inside centre will become just the 10th Springboks centurion when the whistle blows at Ellis Park, with Jean de Villiers the only midfielder before him to reach the milestone.

The achievement puts even more on the line in Saturday’s historic Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series opener, in which De Allende will link up with familiar midfield partner Jesse Kriel to take on New Zealand’s Jordie Barrett and Quinn Tupaea.

Rugby.title: Jona Nareki on the All Blacks' new 'beast', Otago's new star and Wellington's woes
Rugby.summary: For Otago winger Jona Nareki, losing the Ranfurly Shield to Canterbury and then also to Manawatu in the same week would have been intolerable.
Rugby.body:
For Otago winger Jona Nareki, losing the Ranfurly Shield to Canterbury and then also to Manawatu in the same week would have been intolerable. But after a narrow 19-15 loss to Canterbury in Dunedin on Sunday, the prospect of a Palmerston North stumble was real. The visitors trailed 24-7 after 45 minutes and 27-12 with ten minutes left.

“I’m getting older, in rugby age only. I’m not proud of my yellow card coming in the side. I owned one for the team,” Nareki laughed with RugbyPass. “Watching the game from the sideline, I noticed we weren’t winning contact at all while Manawatu went two phases the same way then switched short side to expose us. Once we fixed that, they became easier to defend against.

Rugby.title: The All Blacks' selection policy just got a lot less sentimental
Rugby.summary: Seniority and sentiment became part and parcel of the New Zealand team under previous coaching regimes. Never mind that blokes were plainly not up to it anymore, their status seemed to guarantee them selection.
Rugby.body:
I have to say I’m relieved and optimistic. The first name I looked for, in the All Blacks’ 23 to play South Africa at Ellis Park, was Beauden Barrett. Seniority and sentiment became part and parcel of the New Zealand team under previous coaching regimes. Never mind that blokes were plainly not up to it anymore, their status seemed to guarantee them selection.

So, there’s no Beauden Barrett and no Rieko Ioane in the 23 either. Both are hugely encouraging signs that, while there’s a cast of thousands on this tour, Test caps will still have to be earned.

Rugby.title: 'Borderline Personality Disorder is my superpower'
Rugby.summary: Wales' Donna Rose tells BBC Sport how rugby union has helped her manage Borderline Personality Disorder.
Rugby.body:
Tighthead prop Donna Rose has had an unforgettable 12 months on the rugby pitch. Last year, she proudly represented Wales at her second World Cup before helping Saracens lift the Premiership Women's Rugby title in June.

From the outside looking in, she is known as a hard-hitting player with a big personality. But off the pitch, few see the daily struggles the 35-year-old copes with. Rose has borderline personality disorder (BPD), a mental health condition that causes unstable moods, behaviours and relationships.

Rugby.summary: Fit at long last and selected to start in his familiar No.9 jersey, Roigard says his Springboks sequel has been a long time coming.
Rugby.body:
A run of poorly timed injuries has kept Cam Roigard from lacing up his boots in the famous All Blacks v Springboks rivalry for every showdown since his debut season, with just a brief showing off the bench in his rookie year the exception. This weekend at Ellis Park, the star halfback will finally get his shot at the world champs.

Roigard’s lone showing against South Africa came in a historic defeat at Twickenham ahead of the 2023 Rugby World Cup. Then just 22 years of age, the rising star produced a brilliant solo effort try, one that saved his side from a historic goose egg.

Ellis has previously played in the outside backs for the Wallaroos, debuting for the national team as a winger against the Black Ferns in Wellington last July. But the utility back will wear the No. 10 jersey this weekend, in what will be the 100th Test in Wallaroos history.

Ellis has previously played in the outside backs for the Wallaroos, debuting for the national team as a winger against the Black Ferns in Wellington last July. But the utility back will wear the No. 10 jersey this weekend, in what will be the 100th Test in Wallaroos history.

Rugby.title: ‘Inspire the next generation’: Northland end near 50-year Shield wait
Rugby.summary: Northland have brought an end to a Ranfurly Shield drought that stretches back almost 50 years, leaving players visibly emotional at full-time.
Rugby.body:
Northland have brought an end to a Ranfurly Shield drought that stretches back almost 50 years, leaving players visibly emotional after a famous 35-12 win over Canterbury that was unforgettable in more ways than one.

It was a history-making night at One NZ Stadium for the Taniwha, who hadn’t beaten Canterbury in Christchurch since the late 1980s. All Blacks Sevens star Rob Rush shone bright as Northland ended a long-running search for the Shield as well, which dates back to the 1970s.

Rugby.title: ‘We can win this game’: Wallaroos chase historic first against Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: 30 Tests have been played between the Wallaroos and Black Ferns since September 1994, with the New Zealanders emerging victorious every time.
Rugby.body:
30 Tests have been played between the Wallaroos and Black Ferns since September 1994, with the New Zealanders emerging victorious every time. But the Aussies aren’t shying away from their shot at history, heading across the ditch with the belief “that we can win this game.”

The Wallaroos fell to a 35-point defeat in the last meeting between the rivals on April 25, in a historic Anzac Day fixture between the sides on the Sunshine Coast. Siokapesi Palu Sekona was the sole try-scorer for the Wallaroos, as the Black Ferns retained the O’Reilly Cup.

Rugby.title: News and updates
Rugby.summary: News and updates The Premier of Queensland
Rugby.body:
Queensland is the new home of Australia’s Rugby Sevens and the Wallaroos, after the Queensland Government secured their relocation to the Sunshine State as part of a mega-deal with Rugby Australia which includes a major upgrade of Ballymore and ANZAC Day Bledisloe tests.

In the latest major sporting coup by the Queensland Government, which continues to aggressively raid other states for major events, up to 90 Rugby Australia athletes and staff will move to Queensland from New South Wales to have the Sevens and Wallaroos headquartered in Queensland.

Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus has shared his expectations of the lineout battle in this weekend's Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test series opener, highlighting the tactics and personnel both sides have that will make the contest especially competitive.
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus has shared his expectations for the lineout battle in this weekend’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Test series opener, highlighting the tactics and personnel on both sides that will make the contest especially competitive.

Erasmus’ Springboks famously pride themselves on their set-piece, but with the All Blacks fighting fire with fire by naming two locks over the height of 203 cm in the second row and Tupou Vaa’i on the blindside flank, New Zealand are positioning themselves to be as disruptive as possible in the lineout at Ellis Park.

Rugby.title: Northampton Saints' Archie McParland set for crunch talks over club future
Rugby.summary: Northampton Saints scrum-half Archie McParland is set to have crunch talks about his future with the Gallagher Prem champions after entering the final year of his contract.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints scrum-half Archie McParland is set to have crunch talks about his future with the Gallagher Prem champions after entering the final year of his contract. Saints have started to tie down their players who are out of contract at the end of the forthcoming season and have already made England star Tommy Freeman the highest-paid winger in the league.

They are also set to meet with McParland’s Stowe School team-mate Henry Pollock’s advisors to try to thrash out a new deal that won’t be cheap, even though it is likely to fall short of the headline-grabbing £1 million that his commercial advisor, Eddie Hearn, thinks he is worth.

Rugby.title: Australia's Rugby Sevens Squads Relocate to Brisbane Ahead of 2032 Olympic Games
Rugby.summary: Australia's Rugby Sevens Squads Relocate to Brisbane Ahead of 2032 Olympic Games Fanatik
Rugby.body:
Australia's Rugby Sevens programs will relocate to a new state-of-the-art training facility at Brisbane's Ballymore Stadium complex ahead of the 2032 Olympics, the Queensland government announced on Thursday. The major infrastructure development marks a strategic shift for national rugby operations in Australia.

The new "Teams in Gold Facility" is set to be constructed as part of the broader redevelopment of Ballymore, historically recognized as the spiritual home of rugby union in Queensland. Once construction is complete, both national Sevens teams will move their base from New South Wales to their new Queensland home.

Rugby.title: 'We could have selected him': Erasmus explains Siya Kolisi decision
Rugby.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has revealed that captain Siya Kolisi was available to face the All Blacks this weekend at Ellis Park in the first match of the Greatest Rivalry series, but the coaching team opted against selecting him.
Rugby.body:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has revealed that captain Siya Kolisi was available to face the All Blacks this weekend at Ellis Park in the first match of the Greatest Rivalry series, but the coaching team opted against selecting him.

It was originally feared that the 100-cap veteran would miss a large chunk, if not all, of the highly-anticipated series after picking up a hamstring injury in the Springboks’ 17-10 victory over Argentina earlier this month. However, Erasmus gave an upbeat update earlier this week on the injury status of both Kolisi and loosehead prop Ox Nche, saying they were both in contention to face the All Blacks in Johannesburg.

Rugby.title: Exeter Chiefs 'delighted' as familiar face confirmed as new head coach
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs have promoted Oli Bishop to the role of head coach prior to the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby campaign.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs have promoted Oli Bishop to the role of head coach prior to the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby campaign. Bishop joined the Devon club last summer as attack and backs coach, and had prior PWR coaching experience with London clubs Trailfinders Women and Wasps Women.

In his first season, Bishop implemented one of the most exciting attacks in the English women’s top flight. As the club returned to the play-offs at the first time of asking, Exeter scored 82 tries [third-most in the league] and bagged 14 try-scoring bonus points [joint-second].

Rugby.summary: Premiership Women's Rugby side Exeter Chiefs appoint assistant Oli Bishop as head coach to replace Steve Salvin.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs women have appointed Oli Bishop as their new head coach to replace Steve Salvin who left in July. Bishop has been promoted internally after working as Salvin's assistant coach last season.

Salvin led the Chiefs to third place in the 2025-2026 Premiership Women's Rugby before they lost narrowly to Saracens in the play-off semi-final. He has since left to become full-time forwards coach with Wales after fulfilling the role on an interim basis for the 2026 Six Nations.

Rugby.summary: Stuart McInally made a career out of launching Scotland's lineout ball skywards but now the former hooker is sending something considerably bigger...
Rugby.body:
Stuart McInally made a career out of launching Scotland’s lineout ball skywards but now the former hooker is sending something considerably bigger into the air after swapping professional rugby for a career in the cockpit.

The 34-year-old, who retired from professional rugby in 2023 following a decorated career with Scotland and Edinburgh, has realised a lifelong ambition by joining Jet2, where he’ll be piloting 40 t0nne 737s around Europe’s skies.

Rugby.title: Bok-great's prediction for RGR series doesn't bode well for All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Gary Teichmann has delivered a verdict that All Blacks supporters won't enjoy hearing ahead of the Test segment of the inaugural Greatest Rugby Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Gary Teichmann has delivered a verdict that All Blacks supporters won’t enjoy hearing ahead of the Test segment of the inaugural Greatest Rugby Rivalry series. The former Springbok captain, who led South Africa during New Zealand’s landmark 1996 series win on South African soil, believes Rassie Erasmus’ current world champions are primed to turn the tables 30 years on, backing the Boks to claim a dominant victory – with a caveat.

Speaking in Johannesburg at the launch of the new RGR trophy alongside former All Blacks skipper Sean Fitzpatrick, Teichmann said the memories of that painful 1996 defeat still remain fresh.

Rugby.title: Ex-England U20 back-row Kofi Cripps leaves Bristol to reunite with former coach
Rugby.summary: Champ Rugby champions Worcester Warriors have signed former England U20 back-row Kofi Cripps from Bristol Bears ahead of the new season.
Rugby.body:
Champ Rugby champions Worcester Warriors have signed former England U20 back-row Kofi Cripps from Bristol Bears ahead of the new season. The 23-year-old spent the past year-and-a-half at Ashton Gate, making his Gallagher PREM debut against Newcastle Red Bulls in April, but has had limited game time in the West Country.

The step down to England’s second division will see Cripps reunite with Warriors boss Matt Everard, whom he was coached by earlier in his career at Wasps. Worcester will get their title defence underway in just under a month, hosting Bedford Blues on Saturday, September 19, in what will be a repeat of last season’s final.

Rugby.title: Sana Govender: The Leinster head coach who came by way of Gdansk and Skibbereen
Rugby.summary: When Erin King and Eve Higgins lined out against Munster, earlier this month, it was for the first time as a members of Leinster’s senior squad.
Rugby.body:
When Erin King and Eve Higgins lined out against Munster, earlier this month, it was for the first time as a members of Leinster’s senior squad. It was the same case for Stacey Flood, when she started against Connacht last weekend. All three women have proudly represented Ireland in sevens and XVs, over the past few years [Flood made her senior sevens bow in 2015] yet were part of a large crop winning Leinster debuts.

The drive to get meaningful games into the four senior provinces has led to the recent prominence of the Vodafone Interprovincial Championship. The big stars missed out, last season, as they were on Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 duty, in England. For the current campaign, there have been a raft of overdue debuts.

Rugby.title: Match official appointments locked in for WXV Global Series and Challenger
Rugby.summary: French referee Aurélie Groizeleau will become the fourth female to referee 50 Test matches during the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
French referee Aurélie Groizeleau will become the fourth female to referee 50 Test matches during the WXV Global Series presented by Mitsubishi Electric. She joins Matthew Carley (England), Aimee Barrett-Theron (South Africa) and Hollie Davidson (Scotland) in reaching the landmark this year, and is the fifth French official to achieve the feat.

Groizeleau is one of 10 Emirates Match Officials appointed by World Rugby to take charge of the 30 WXV Global Series 2026 fixtures taking place across 13 counties. The 37-year-old will take charge of the opening game of the WXV Global Series campaign between England and Australia in Salford and hit her half-century the following month when she takes charge of Canada’s clash with the Red Roses in Toronto.

Rugby.summary: Alex Davies joins Steve Tandy's Wales management team as kicking coach after leaving Leicester.
Rugby.body:
Alex Davies is leaving Leicester to join Wales' management team as kicking coach. Steve Tandy has appointed the 40-year-old after being helped by Rhys Patchell and Leigh Halfpenny in his first campaign as head coach.

Davies, a former half-back, spent last season full-time with Leicester after previously working with the Netherlands, Rosslyn Park and England women. He will work with the Wales men's national team during Test windows and coach individuals throughout the season, while also helping age-grade players.

Rugby.title: Northland end 48-year Ranfurly Shield drought with win over Canterbury
Rugby.summary: Northland have won the Ranfurly Shield for the first time since 1979 and claimed their first win in Christchurch since the late 1980s.
Rugby.body:
Northland have won the Ranfurly Shield for the first time in 48 years and claimed their first win in Christchurch since the late 1980s, taking down Canterbury 31-12 on a history-making night for the Taniwha at One NZ Stadium.

Canterbury claimed ‘The Log of Wood’ with a nail-biting four-point win over Otago in round two before successfully defending the Shield with another hard-earned 33-28 triumph over Bay of Plenty last weekend.

Rugby.title: Who is best equipped to strike first in the Greatest Rivalry showdown?
Rugby.summary: Are the world champion Springboks or new-look All Blacks in pole position to win their hugely anticipated first Test on Saturday?
Rugby.body:
“Every battle is won or lost before it is fought”. That pithy saying by the Chinese warrior-philosopher Sun-Tzu has become an axiom of modern sport at the elite level. The winning tends to consist of the preparation: the logistics on the approach-road to battle, the detail of the planning, the precision of the fore-knowledge of the strengths and weaknesses on both sides, observed without bias.

That is the process Rassie Erasmus and Dave Rennie, the rival head coaches of South Africa and New Zealand, will be fine-tuning now. The battle will only be fought at 17:10 on Saturday at Ellis Park, but there are myriad is to be dotted and ts to be crossed before then – in selection, in game planning, and in physical and mental training.

Rugby.title: Why Wallaroos coach has ‘no doubt’ Maddison Levi is ready for Test debut
Rugby.summary: Wallaroos assistant coach Mike Ruthven has complete confidence in Levi, expecting the SVNS star to “do really well” in 15s.
Rugby.body:
HSBC SVNS Series phenom Maddison Levi is in line to debut for the Wallaroos against the Black Ferns, without having played any Super Rugby Women’s. But Wallaroos assistant coach Mike Ruthven has complete confidence in Levi, expecting the SVNS star to “do really well” in 15s.

Levi has signed on to play in the inaugural Ultimate Sevens season, before the 2027 HSBC SVNS Series gets underway in late November, but will first get the chance to feature for the Wallaroos in an O’Reilly Cup Test in Auckland.

Rugby.title: Australia's Rugby Sevens squads to move to Brisbane ahead of 2032 Games
Rugby.summary: Australia's Rugby Sevens squads to move to Brisbane ahead of 2032 Games CNA
Rugby.body:
SYDNEY, Aug 20 : Australia's Rugby Sevens programmes will move to a new state-of-the-art training facility at Brisbane's Ballymore Stadium complex ahead of the 2032 Olympics in the city, the Queensland government said on Thursday.

The "Teams in Gold Facility" will be built as part of the redevelopment of Ballymore, which is the traditional home of rugby union in the state and once hosted World Cup, test and top provincial matches.

Rugby.title: Australia Sevens, Wallaroos to call Ballymore home with ‘Teams of Gold’ upgrade
Rugby.summary: Australia’s Sevens program is set to have a new home with Queensland Rugby’s spiritual home of Ballymore set for a colossal upgrade.
Rugby.body:
Australia’s Sevens program is set to have a new home in the Sunshine State, with Queensland Rugby’s spiritual home of Ballymore set for a colossal upgrade ahead of the 2032 Olympics.

As part of a new partnership between Rugby Australia, the Queensland Rugby Union and the Queensland Government, the move will see the stadium as the permanent, year-round home for both the men’s and women’s high performance programs, relocating from Moore Park in Sydney.

Rugby.title: Ex-Wallaby’s telling observation before Taniela Tupou’s two-try heroics
Rugby.summary: Stan Sport commentator Morgan Turinui noticed Taniela Tupou’s “physical presence” during the Wallabies’ warm-up on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Stan Sport commentator Morgan Turinui noticed Taniela Tupou’s “physical presence” during the Wallabies’ warm-up on Saturday, before the front-rower went on to score two tries in a 56-17 win over the Brave Blossoms in Townsville.

Tupou crashed over for a crucial try as the Wallabies prevailed over the same opponent 35-32 a week earlier in Osaka, and was then brought into the national team’s starting side for the first time since November 23.

Rugby.title: Ex-All Black captain Read says Argentina gave the 'blueprint' for Boks
Rugby.summary: Ex-All Black captain Kieran Read believes that Argentina provided the blueprint for beating the Springboks in Buenos Aires a fortnight ago.
Rugby.body:
Ex-All Black captain Kieran Read believes that Argentina provided the blueprint for beating the Springboks in Buenos Aires a fortnight ago. Los Pumas hosted a strong South Africa side, although missing a host of topline stars, and were able to trouble them in their 17-10 loss, missing the chance to draw level with the final play of the game.

They led 10-3 for most of the first half and created a number of opportunities out wide through a varied attacking game that implemented chips and cross-field kicks. “Even though they [South Africa] didn’t put anything on the table in Argentina, Argentina showed us exactly how we should try to beat the Springboks,” Read said on The Good, The Bad & Rugby ANZ podcast.

Rugby.title: 'Not here for a sugar hit': Waratahs expect sustained success from 'proven winner' Cheika
Rugby.summary: NSW Waratahs staff have been placed on notice to expect a rude awakening when Michael Cheika returns as coach.
Rugby.body:
From the board down to the players and his assistants, all NSW Waratahs staff have been placed on notice to expect a rude awakening when Michael Cheika returns as coach. A proven force of nature, “Cyclone Cheika” will officially arrive at Daceyville in November charged with restoring the Waratahs to the glory days after three years without a Super Rugby Pacific finals appearance and a decade of under-achieving since he left the first time.

The firebrand mentor led the Waratahs to their one and only championship in 2014, while his abrasive style has also brought success to almost every team he’s coached. Cheika also coached Leinster to European Cup glory, Argentina to the World Cup semi-finals for the first time in 2023 and, as an assistant to Trent Robinson, has helped put the Sydney Roosters on track to claiming this year’s NRL minor premiership.

Rugby.title: Ranking 21 England back-row options ahead of the 2026/27 season
Rugby.summary: This time next year, Steve Borthwick will be very close to finalising his squad for the 2027 World Cup in Australia, and the back-row will be the cause of many sleepless nights.
Rugby.body:
This time next year, Steve Borthwick will be very close to finalising his squad for the 2027 World Cup in Australia, and the back-row will be the cause of many sleepless nights.

A lot has changed since ranking England’s back-row options last year – not only did Borthwick lose his preferred No.8 Tom Willis, who has joined his brother, Jack, in France, but a midseason shift in the back-row make-up occurred following a manhandling at the hands of Ireland at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium. This was all just a minor subplot in a season where England’s results took a dramatic dive.

Rugby.title: All Blacks and Springboks agree to drawn series scenario
Rugby.summary: The Springboks and All Blacks have agreed that in the event of a drawn series in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour, there will be no tiebreaker, leaving the series as a draw.
Rugby.body:
The Springboks and All Blacks have agreed that in the event of a drawn series in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour, there will be no tiebreaker, leaving the series as a draw. Wednesday afternoon’s trophy launch event in Johannesburg revealed the decision, as former Springboks captain Gary Teichmann carried one half of the sculptural trophy through a crowd and onto the stage, followed shortly after by former All Blacks captain Sean Fitzpatrick with the other half.

Once on stage, the pair pressed the two pieces of the trophy together, revealing how magnets join them to form a single trophy, which would be handed to the winner of the series should either side claim at least three wins.

Rugby.title: Why Rassie’s next Bok generation could be the greatest ever
Rugby.summary: The Springbok dynasty doesn't look like it is going to disappear any time soon and it could, in fact, get even stronger in future
Rugby.body:
I’m positively hyperventilating about The Greatest Rivalry Test Series and it has my mind doing overtime as to how many ways it could go. It may be a heatwave here in the UK but over in South Africa, it’s piping hot for another reason. As ever, when it comes to rugby, there is no off-switch and this is what has been on my mind over the last month.

Sometimes the “next generation” can be a bit of letdown. Whether it’s people or products, the next in line doesn’t always mean an improvement. If you’ve ever spent a £1,000 on a new phone in recent years, or you’re acquainted with royal history over the past 1,000 years, you’ll know succession doesn’t always equal success — King John of England was arguably the iPhone 6 Plus of monarchs. However, the next generation of Rassie’s Springboks could arguably be the best to ever do it. They simply have to be, and for one reason: if you aren’t an almost generational-level player, you simply don’t get to play in the Test team proper.

Rugby.title: 'Big step forward': Springbok Women name squad for inaugural 'A' tour
Rugby.summary: SA Rugby have confirmed the 26-player squad that will travel to Brazil for the first-ever South Africa Women 'A' tour.
Rugby.body:
SA Rugby have confirmed the 26-player squad that will travel to Brazil for the first-ever South Africa Women ‘A’ tour. They will play Brazil ‘A’ squad in back-to-back fixtures in Sao Paolo on 24 and 29 August. The squad will be captained by capped Springbok Women back Mary Zulu, who represented the Boks at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

The 23-year-old is one of capped Springbok players in the playing group travelling to South America, which boasts an average age of 22. Luchell Hanekom, who also competed in England last year, returns from injury.

Rugby.title: Jake White: I urge Rennie to make a huge call that won't go down well in NZ
Rugby.summary: The hours are counting down to the first Test in Johannesburg and whisper it, but the portents are shaping up well for the All Blacks. The stars are aligning.
Rugby.body:
The hours are counting down to the first Test in Johannesburg and whisper it, but the portents are shaping up well for the All Blacks. The stars are aligning. I’ll explain. If you were a rugby coach, and you were asked if you wanted to coach international rugby, the answer would be yes. Now, if you were then asked to pick any side in the world to coach most, without hesitation, would say South Africa, France, maybe England, but you can bet your bottom dollar New Zealand would be right up there. A year out from the World Cup, you’re asked where would your dream tour would be? South Africa, the year before the World Cup? Consider it done. For good measure, we’ll throw in a couple of friendlies, an extended 45-man squad and you can tour the Republic, play golf, go to game farms and have an incredible bonding opportunity. Oh, and we’ll make those warm-up games winnable and schedule the last game at altitude to replicate the first Test. Of course, you can play the Bulls. What’s not to like?

What I’m saying is Dave Rennie has nothing to complain about. It’s the perfect scenario. They are unbeaten. They have a new coach. They have renewed energy. They’ve been given the opportunity of an extended tour, playing the world champions, who are likely to be in their way in their quest to win a fourth World Cup, and they’re underdogs. They are in a helluva good place.

Rugby.title: Spain announce one-off Test against rising women's rugby nation
Rugby.summary: Spain's Las Leonas will play a one-off Test against the Springbok Women at the start of October.
Rugby.body:
Spain’s Las Leonas will play a one-off Test against the Springbok Women at the start of October. The fixture will take place shortly after the side has played WXV Global Series Challenger fixtures against Fiji, Samoa and Brazil in Hong Kong China.

Seville will host the match at its La Cartuja Sports Complex on Sunday 4 October. It will be the first time that Las Leonas have ever played a fixture in the city. In their release, Real Federación Española de Rugby [FER] claimed that their first home game of the season will be “crucial for the women’s national team’s objectives; with qualification for the 2029 World Cup in Australia potentially within reach this season”.

Rugby.title: Wales sports minister meets WRU after fans' fears
Rugby.summary: Wales' sports minister Heledd Fychan meets with Welsh Rugby Union to express fears of split with fans over three-team plan.
Rugby.body:
Wales' sports minister has met with the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) after concerns of a "disconnect" between the governing body and fans. The WRU has doubled down in recent weeks on plans to cut a professional men's side, with Scarlets or Ospreys set to be culled by 2028.

Heledd Fychan MS, the Senedd's chief whip and cabinet minister for culture and sport, insisted the WRU is an independent organisation and Welsh government has no direct role in its decision-making.

Heledd Fychan MS, the Senedd's chief whip and cabinet minister for culture and sport, insisted the WRU is an independent organisation and Welsh government has no direct role in its decision-making.

Rugby.title: Cardiff sign Leicester lock Manz on loan
Rugby.summary: Cardiff strengthen pack ahead of 2026-27 season by signing Leicester lock Tom Manz on loan.
Rugby.body:
Cardiff have strengthened their second-row options by signing Leicester's Tom Manz on a season-long loan. The 6ft 8in lock, who featured 10 times for Tigers last season, will spend the 2026-27 campaign in the United Rugby Championship (URC).

Cardiff made the play-offs last season despite being stretched in the second row. After missing out on Wales international Christ Tshiunza to Sale, they have signed Tongan Semisi Paea and now 24-year-old Manz.

Rugby.title: All Blacks great accuses Rassie Erasmus of 'conspiracy'
Rugby.summary: Former All Blacks wing John Kirwan has suggested that South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus instructed the provincial sides to "not play like the Springboks" against the All Blacks in order to "lull them into a false sense of security" ahead of the Test series.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks wing John Kirwan has suggested that South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus instructed the provincial sides to “not play like the Springboks” against the All Blacks in order to “lull them into a false sense of security” ahead of the Test series.

The All Blacks head into their first Test against the Springboks this Saturday at Ellis Park off the back of wins over the Stormers, Sharks and Bulls, with all three matches far from resembling Test match rugby.

Rugby.title: New Zealand great Tui joins Trailfinders
Rugby.summary: World Cup-winning New Zealand international Ruby Tui, 34, signs a one-year deal with Trailfinders Women.
Rugby.body:
World Cup-winning New Zealand international Ruby Tui has signed for Trailfinders Women. BBC Sport understands Tui, 34, has agreed a one-year deal with last season's Premiership Women's Rugby finalists.

"Ruby is one of the most respected figures in the women's game," Trailfinders head coach Barney Maddison told the club's website, external. "Her experience of winning at the very highest level, combined with the energy and leadership she brings off the pitch, will be an enormous asset to the squad as we push on from last season."

Rugby.title: Atlanta Lolohea: 'My rugby is the most settled it’s been'
Rugby.summary: Established in 1861, Westport is New Zealand's oldest European settlement on the West Coast. Best known as a coal-mining centre, Westport has a population of less than 5000.
Rugby.body:
Established in 1861, Westport is New Zealand’s oldest European settlement on the West Coast. Best known as a coal-mining centre, Westport has a population of less than 5000. Still, it produces big dreamers and champions, including Black Ferns hooker Atlanta Lolohea, named after the sprawling American city in Georgia; home to the world’s largest airport, the 1996 Olympic Games, and known for casinos, Coca-Cola, blues and hip-hop music. It is also where an older sister was performing when Lolohea was born.

Lolohea has played 11 Tests for New Zealand but only 13 Farah Palmer Cup games for Canterbury, winning 11, including a Premiership in 2022. For most of her career she has been an understudy to the more experienced Georgia Ponsonby. Could that be set to change?

Rugby.title: Asia Rugby Sevens Series returns with new contenders chasing title honours
Rugby.summary: The headlining event, the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series (ARESS 2026) is set to feature 12 women’s and 12 men’s teams.
Rugby.body:
August to October are set to be busy months in Asia, with the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series and U18s tournaments set to get underway across China and Sri Lanka. The headlining event, the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series (ARESS 2026) is set to feature 12 women’s and 12 men’s teams, with the two events taking place either side of the 2026 Asian Games taking in Aichi & Nagoya, Japan, which will also feature several sides.

Suzhou in China is set to host the first weekend of action on the final weekend of August, with the tournament set to feature two newly promoted sides in both the men’s and women’s tournaments.

Rugby.title: KCB send strong message to Kenya Nations 7s Circuit rivals
Rugby.summary: The domestic sevens competition in Kenya is heating up, with defending champions KCB sending a strong message to the rest of the competition.
Rugby.body:
The domestic sevens competition in Kenya is heating up, with defending champions KCB sending a strong message to the rest of the competition with victory at the Kabeberi 7s. Heading into the third leg of the National 7s Circuit, the official halfway point of the competition, the defending champions had claimed victory in the opening round at the Prinsloo Sevens, before collapsing to finish in fifth at the Dala Sevens a fortnight ago.

However, spearheaded by Kenyan HSBC SVNS sarts George Ooro and Mike Wekesa, KCB fired back emphatically at the RFUEA Grounds in Nairobi, sweeping through their pool stages and claiming the final in a tense 14-12 win over Strathmore Leos.

Rugby.title: The SVNS Series stars already shaping the race to LA 2028
Rugby.summary: Some names already look almost certain to be central to that conversation. Others are only just beginning to emerge.
Rugby.body:
It may be too early to talk about Olympic favourites and the road to Los Angeles 2028 has barely begun, but a number of sevens’ biggest names are already giving us a glimpse of who could define the next cycle.

There is something different about an Olympic cycle in rugby sevens. The four-year countdown can feel impossibly long when the next Games are still two summers away, but in a sport where careers can change at remarkable speed, reputations are already being built.

Rugby.title: ‘Score one try against the All Blacks and your life is made’: Three great Springbok tries v NZ
Rugby.summary: Thinus Delport, Richard Bands and Ricky Januarie all achieved rugby immortality with career-defining tries against New Zealand.
Rugby.body:
There are worse things than being remembered for the best ten seconds of your life. Richard Bands has won Currie Cups, played Test rugby for South Africa and built a second career teaching young props the mysteries of the scrum. More than two decades after his last Springbok appearance, none of that is usually the first thing people want to discuss.

“I’m more than chuffed,” Bands says. “In my career, I’ve created something that 23 years later, when I speak to people, they still can tell me exactly where they were watching that game, watching me score that try.”

Rugby.title: Ruby Tui’s club future revealed after fortnight of social media clues
Rugby.summary: Speculation around Ruby Tui's club future has been put to rest after she signed for JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby runners-up Trailfinders Women.
Rugby.body:
Speculation around Ruby Tui‘s club future has been put to rest after she signed for JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby runners-up Trailfinders Women. Across the past two weeks the Black Ferns wing and Rugby World Cup 2021 winner teased that her time on a rugby pitch may not have been over on her social media channels.

In June the 34-year-old played her first game of 15-a-side rugby in almost a year for the Barbarians against Wales at Allianz Stadium. In an exclusive interview with The Telegraph, Tui confessed that it took some persuading from some women’s rugby greats to convince her not to hang up her boots: “My friends Portia Woodman-Wickliffe and Meg Jones helped me, [they] really had a massive input on making the decision.

Rugby.summary: An Eagles-heavy USA XV claimed a hard-earned 25-24 win over an Argentina XV at Inter Miami FC Stadium last weekend.
Rugby.body:
An Eagles-heavy USA XV claimed a hard-earned 25-24 win over an Argentina XV at Inter Miami FC Stadium last weekend, which served as a valuable hit out for the playing group 14 months out from Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027.

Shilo Klein, Makeen Alikhan and Marno Redelinghuys all touched down for tries, giving the home side a decent lead with about 10 minutes left on the clock. But the visitors fought their way back, making it a one-point game in the dying stages.

Rugby.summary: Ex-All Black Justin Marshall has responded to the Springbok supporters laying claim to the favourites tag ahead of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Test series, labelling the confidence "arrogance", but stopping short of disputing its validity.

Rugby.title: Michael Cheika returns to Waratahs more than a decade after title triumph
Rugby.summary: Michael Cheika has been unveiled as the NSW Waratahs head coach ahead of the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season.
Rugby.body:
Michael Cheika has been unveiled as the NSW Waratahs head coach ahead of the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season, more than a decade after leading the side to its maiden championship title back in 2014.

Cheika will officially step back into the top role at the Tahs this November, committing to next season with an option for 2028. The former World Rugby Coach of the Year returns to the club with an extensive coaching CV that has spanned multiple countries and a couple of sports.
