Rugby.title: Damian McKenzie 'trending well' as Cortez Ratima still under injury cloud
Rugby.summary: All Blacks fullback Damian McKenzie is heading in the right direction according to assistant coach Tana Umaga as he battles to be fit for the first Test at Ellis Park.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks fullback Damian McKenzie is heading in the right direction according to assistant coach Tana Umaga as he battles to be fit for the first Test at Ellis Park. Umaga confirmed McKenzie got through the required training block on Tuesday as he battles an ankle injury suffered against the Sharks in Durban.

“He was sharp today. He got through what he needed to get through. So, he’s trending well for a big one this weekend. So, that’s all we can ask,” Umaga told media. “Our medical staff has done a really good job, as well as our S&C, to make sure that they’re taking every precaution they can, but making sure that he puts his best foot forward to be available for the team.”

Rugby.title: Ikitau and Suaalii return as Wallabies brace for ‘tough challenge’ in Argentina
Rugby.summary: 2025 John Eales Medal winner Len Ikitau has been named in a 34-man Wallabies squad for Flight Centre Series Tests against Los Pumas.
Rugby.body:
2025 John Eales Medal winner Len Ikitau has been named in a 34-man Wallabies squad for Flight Centre Series Tests against Los Pumas in Argentina, overcoming an ankle injury that ruled the centre out of both matches against the Brave Blossoms.

Ikitau didn’t feature in the first match of the Les Kiss coaching era, which was a thrilling 35-32 win over Japan in Osaka. Both Ikitau and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii missed the Townsville Test, but the Wallabies still prevailed 56-17.

Rugby.summary: Former Crusaders U20s Academy prospect Netani Baleisomosomo has earned an opportunity in Super Rugby Pacific with the Western Force.
Rugby.body:
Former Crusaders U20s Academy prospect Netani Baleisomosomo has earned an opportunity in Super Rugby Pacific with the Western Force, signing a two-year deal with the club after impressing in Queensland Premier Rugby.

Fiji-born Baleisomosomo moved to New Zealand as a teenager on a scholarship with prestigious rugby nursery Nelson College. The loose forward has later been a part of the Crusaders U20s system and the Tasman Mako squad at the provincial level.

Rugby.title: Australian-born USA Eagles prop seals France move as medical joker
Rugby.summary: USA Eagles prop Charlie Abel has sealed a return to European rugby 10 years after first playing in France, signing with Pro D2 outfit Oyonnax Rugby.
Rugby.body:
USA Eagles prop Charlie Abel has sealed a return to European rugby 10 years after first playing in France, signing with Pro D2 outfit Oyonnax Rugby as a medical joker. The Australian-born front-rower has been added to the squad after tighthead Ali Oz picked up a hamstring injury.

Abel debuted for the USA national team during the inaugural World Rugby Nations Cup fixtures last month, coming off the bench in a win over Spain. The Eagles secured an unbeaten 3-0 record in July after sides all bound for Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 in Australia.

Rugby.title: Dave Rennie reveals Rassie Erasmus turned down pre-match meeting with officials
Rugby.summary: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie revealed that the coaches will not be having any pre-match meetings with the match officials after Rassie Erasmus declined.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie revealed that the coaches will not be having any pre-match meetings with the match officials after Rassie Erasmus declined the meeting. Under the new World Rugby protocols, head coaches may only meet with a referee before a Test match if both opposing head coaches accept the invitation and attend the meeting together.

Erasmus’ decision to decline the meeting appears at odds with the media approach adopted by the Springboks which has been to raise discussions around the laws. Jaco Peyper was brought out to a press conference to explain the 30-second formation rule, while assistant Felix Jones aired the grievances of the South African club teams had against the All Blacks.

Rugby.title: Maisy Allen steps out of 'comfort zone' with short-term move
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs vice-captain Maisy Allen will join Canterbury for the upcoming Farah Palmer Cup campaign in New Zealand.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs vice-captain Maisy Allen will join Canterbury for the upcoming Farah Palmer Cup campaign in New Zealand. The flanker – who won the last of her five caps for the Red Roses against the Black Ferns at WXV 1 in 2023 – will return to her JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club for the start of the English league season in November.

Canterbury, who were runners-up last year, start their season against the Auckland Storm in a fortnight’s time. She made 17 league appearances as Chiefs returned to the play-offs at the first time of asking. Across her 1231 match minutes, Allen scored 10 tries, carried the ball 153 times for 545 metres, beat 29 defenders, completed 249 tackles and won 15 turnovers.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Bok coach publicly raises alarm over illegal All Blacks acts 'the franchises weren't happy with'
Rugby.summary: Springboks assistant coach Felix Jones has raised concerns over the legality of the All Blacks' tactics after receiving feedback from the South African franchises.
Rugby.body:
Springboks assistant coach Felix Jones has raised concerns over the legality of the All Blacks‘ tactics after receiving feedback from the South African franchises. The All Blacks have faced the Stormers, the Sharks and the Bulls in the opening three matches of their Greatest Rivalry series, recording three victories in the process ahead of the first Test against Rassie Erasmus’ side on Saturday at Ellis Park.

Speaking to the media ahead of the much-anticipated encounter in Johannesburg, Jones revealed some of the feedback the Springboks have received from the franchises after their encounters with the All Blacks. The Bok coaching staff have seen plenty that confirmed their own observations from the Nations Championship, particularly in how New Zealand are looking to play, but Jones said “a couple of things caught the franchises out”.

Rugby.title: Announcement imminent of Michael Cheika's rugby union return
Rugby.summary: Former Wallabies boss Michael Cheika is set for a sensational return to the NSW Waratahs after calling time on his bid to become an NRL head coach.
Rugby.body:
Former Wallabies boss Michael Cheika is set for a sensational return to the NSW Waratahs after calling time on his bid to become an NRL head coach. Cheika has spent this season working as an assistant coach at the Sydney Roosters on a one-year deal, after returning to Australia following a spell in the Gallagher Prem with Leicester Tigers.

It is 11 years since Cheika, 59, left the Waratahs, whom he led to a Super Rugby title in 2014, to become the full-time Wallabies coach after having done both jobs for 12 months. Since then, they have reached only one semi-final.

Rugby.summary: Tana Umaga says the All Blacks can ill afford to get absorbed by the Springboks' giant pack and lose sight of their backline threats, with the evolution of South Africa's game set to pose a wide array of challenges to the New Zealand defence.
Rugby.body:
Tana Umaga says the All Blacks can ill afford to get absorbed by the Springboks’ giant pack and lose sight of their backline threats, with the evolution of South Africa’s game set to pose a wide array of challenges to the New Zealand defence over the coming month.

Umaga has overseen the All Blacks’ defence portfolio for six games now, conceding an average of 23 points per game against three international opponents in July and 13 against three URC club teams to begin the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour.

Rugby.title: ‘They look vulnerable’: Victor Matfield spots weakness ahead of Boks' first All Blacks clash
Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has said that he "saw something" in the All Blacks' 50-19 win over the Bulls at the weekend that showed a weakness in Dave Rennie's side ahead of their first meeting with the Springboks at Ellis Park on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has said that he “saw something” in the All Blacks‘ 50-19 win over the Bulls at the weekend that showed a weakness in Dave Rennie’s side ahead of their first meeting with the Springboks at Ellis Park on Saturday.

The All Blacks completed their final warm-up match before the Test series with a comfortable win at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday, building a 24-0 half-time lead. As impressive as the visitors were in the first half, the former Springboks lock has said they looked “vulnerable” in the second half as the “pressure came” from United Rugby Championship runners-up.

Rugby.title: How do Australia fit both ‘fetchers’ in side? Could ‘McZano’ be next ‘Pooper’ combo?
Rugby.summary: With two outstanding opensides in Fraser McReight and Carlo Tizzano, Les Kiss has an enviable dilemma to navigate.
Rugby.body:
If there’s one common thread that can be traced through Australian rugby since the dawn of professionalism, it’s been the continual line of genuinely world-class, on-ball openside flankers.

It might even extend well beyond the advent of professionalism in the 1990s, if we’re honest, but there’s no denying the lineage since the game turned pro. It starts with David Wilson in the late 90s and quickly moves to George Smith in that period Australian fans knowingly refer to as the ‘Golden Years’, a period that hasn’t really been replicated since. Annoyingly.

Rugby.title: Alysia Lefau-Fakaosilea reveals what has her ‘excited’ in Wallaroos camp
Rugby.summary: It has been seven years since Alysia Lefau-Fakaosilea last played a Test match for the Wallaroos.
Rugby.body:
It has been seven years since Alysia Lefau-Fakaosilea last played a Test match for the Wallaroos. Just a teenager when handed her first taste of international rugby, in the years since the powerful centre has curated her craft with Australia Sevens and picked up gold medals at the Rugby Sevens World Cup and Commonwealth Games in 2022. But now the 25-year-old has returned to her roots.

Back in the Wallaroos squad ahead of the team’s centenary Test – which will take place against the Black Ferns in Auckland this Saturday – Lefau-Fakaosilea is at the forefront of an ever-changing Australia side. Even if Michaela Leonard and Emily Chancellor remain from her last O’Reilly Cup outing.

Rugby.title: How has the dry weather affected rugby clubs?
Rugby.summary: BBC Sport examines how the drought conditions in England have affected rugby clubs.
Rugby.body:
"Although summers are getting a lot drier, this is by far the driest we've been," says Simon Johnson, the groundsman at National Two side Redruth. Sports pitches up and down the country have been affected by the lack of rainfall, with the south west of England being in a state of drought since the end of July.

A hosepipe ban was implemented earlier this month as little rain fell, causing difficulty for sports fields up and down the country. "The lack of rainfall has affected end-of-season renovations so grass seed hasn't germinated quite as quickly as it should have done," Johnson told BBC Radio Cornwall.

Rugby.summary: TV presenter Nick Knowles believes Cornish Pirates are capable of making the Prem after investing in the club.
Rugby.body:
TV presenter Nick Knowles believes Cornish Pirates are capable of becoming a sustainable Prem club. The presenter of shows such as DIY SOS and National Lottery: Who Dares Wins invested in the Pirates earlier this month.

He is one of a number of new investors to join the Penzance-based Champ club over the past year or so. American firm Stonewood Capital Management took a stake in May to join a consortium of local businessmen who took over the club from long-serving owner Dick Evans in January 2025.

Rugby.title: Wallabies boosted as three outside backs likely to be fit for Argentina
Rugby.summary: Les Kiss will continue to test the limits of his Wallabies unit in Argentina, adamant its more flexible than even the players think.
Rugby.body:
Les Kiss will continue to test the limits of his Wallabies unit in Argentina, adamant its more flexible than even the players think. A squad for the two-Test tour – their first game is in San Salvador on August 29 – is likely to be named on Wednesday.

It’s understood Max Jorgensen, who limped off with sore ribs after a collision in the side’s big Townsville win over Japan on Saturday, will be fit to travel. Centres Len Ikitau (ankle) and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii (hamstring) are also firming for returns, giving their coach more welcome headaches after casting the net wide in his first two games in charge.

Rugby.title: Three-time World Cup player returning home for Super Rugby Pacific
Rugby.summary: The offload specialist has made 132 professional appearances across stints at the Glasgow Warriors, Racing 92, Toulon and Castres, and won 68 Test caps.
Rugby.body:
Three-time World Cup player Leone Nakarawa is returning home to Fiji to play for the Drua in the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific competition. One of the most storied Flying Fijians of all time, Nakarawa is set to bring much-needed experience to the young Drua squad.

As well as being a part of three Rugby World Cup campaigns, including 2015 when he was selected in the official team of the tournament, the 38-year-old was part of their gold medal-winning sevens squad at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

Rugby.title: Hansen forced to draft in two players ahead of ‘pressure’ Wallaroos clash
Rugby.summary: Following the Black Ferns' clash with the Wallaroos, they will travel to South Africa to feature in a double header with the All Blacks in Johannesburg on September 5.
Rugby.body:
Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has been forced to draft in two Black Ferns XV players ahead of their clash with the Wallaroos at Mt Smart Stadium on Saturday evening. The Black Ferns, who beat the Black Ferns XV 62-19 in Upper Hutt last Friday, will take on Australia in Auckland on Saturday to kick-start a busy international period for Hansen’s side.

The Wallaroos will head into the contest without their newly appointed head coach, as Sione Fukofuka is only taking the reins from January 2027. But for Hansen and the Black Ferns, the original squad has changed following the trial match, with both Tara Turner and Mo’omo’oga Palu picking up injuries that have made them unavailable for the weekend.

Rugby.title: Josh Moorby reveals All Blacks’ expectations of Boks amid style debate
Rugby.summary: There's been a tense feel to the first Test week in the Republic, with both coaches responding to and discussing certain narratives surrounding this weekend's showdown at Ellis Park in Johannesburg.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks outside back Josh Moorby isn’t feeding into the narratives around the Springboks possibly slowing the game down ahead of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour. There’s been a tense feel to the first Test week in the Republic, with both coaches responding to and discussing certain narratives surrounding this weekend’s showdown at Ellis Park in Johannesburg.

The All Blacks, who have preached a fast-paced contest, are clear in their intentions to take the game to the Springboks from the get-go in the first Test. One player who will welcome the All Blacks’ high ball-in-play attitude is Moorby, who dotted down for two tries against the Bulls in Pretoria, continuing his exceptional try-scoring form from the 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season.

Rugby.title: 'Always three truths': Rassie Erasmus and Jaco Peyper respond to accusations of slowing the game
Rugby.summary: Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus and technical consultant Jaco Peyper have responded to the narrative that the Springboks want to play a 'slow game' against the All Blacks.
Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus and technical consultant Jaco Peyper have responded to the narrative that the Springboks want to play a ‘slow game’ against the All Blacks.

Peyper revealed that “not once” have the Springboks got feedback that they slow the game down in 2026 following the new protocols for feedback. The former referee who now consults to the Springboks confirmed the law that the Springboks play to, which is that they have 30 seconds from the time the mark is given to form the set piece.

Tennis.title: Why Jack Draper can take plenty of heart from seeing Arthur Fils win the Cincinnati Open
Tennis.summary: Why Jack Draper can take plenty of heart from seeing Arthur Fils win the Cincinnati Open Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Arthur Fils’ Cincinnati Open title was an absolute triumph for tennis, and could prove to be the moment that catapults him towards true greatness within this sport. For years now, people have been speaking about this talented Frenchman as a player more than capable of challenging the established elite, but every time he seemed to be making progress, a new physical issue would emerge.

These problems are not completely gone just yet, but this maiden Masters 1000 triumph marks a well-deserved reward for years of hard work against the odds. Many at home will have been delighted to see Arthur Fils get over the line, as seemingly one of the more well-liked players on the ATP Tour.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper and Axel Arigato Drop 'Midnight,' the Final Sneaker in Their Grand Slam Trilogy
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper and Axel Arigato Drop 'Midnight,' the Final Sneaker in Their Grand Slam Trilogy Complex
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper and Axel Arigato have unveiled “Midnight,” the final chapter in their trilogy of sneaker collaborations. Ahead of the US Open, the UK tennis star is completing the trilogy of collaborations with “Midnight,” a black take on the Dice silhouette with teal accents. Following “Dusk” and “Rise,” the new pair of sneakers celebrates the institution of night sessions. The timing of its release, on Wednesday (Aug. 26), coincides with the start of the US Open, which became the first Grand Slam to play under floodlights in 1975.

“Everything about New York feels bigger at night,” said Jack Draper of the final sneaker collaboration in the trilogy. “The city, the noise, those late sessions—it’s got that Gotham energy I’ve always loved. Midnight is the shoe for that: dark, sharp, made for after hours. It felt like the only way to finish the trilogy.”
Tennis.copy:
Jack Draper and Axel Arigato have unveiled “Midnight,” the final chapter in their trilogy of sneaker collaborations. Ahead of the US Open, the UK tennis star is completing the trilogy of collaborations with “Midnight,” a black take on the Dice silhouette with teal accents. Following “Dusk” and “Rise,” the new pair of sneakers celebrates the institution of night sessions. The timing of its release, on Wednesday (Aug. 26), coincides with the start of the US Open, which became the first Grand Slam to play under floodlights in 1975.

“Everything about New York feels bigger at night,” said Jack Draper of the final sneaker collaboration in the trilogy. “The city, the noise, those late sessions—it’s got that Gotham energy I’ve always loved. Midnight is the shoe for that: dark, sharp, made for after hours. It felt like the only way to finish the trilogy.”

Coco Gauff defeated fellow American Jessica Pegula in straight sets, 6-2 6-4, to capture her second Cincinnati Open women's singles title. It means the world No 4 becomes just the third player in the Open Era, after Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka, to win multiple titles in Cincinnati.

Frenchman Arthur Fils may have played himself into contention to win the US Open after sealing the biggest title of his career at the Cincinnati Open on Sunday. The 21st seed, who won the Barcelona Open in April, added the Cincy crown to his growing list of achievements with a topsy-turvy 6-3 1-6 6-0 victory over Frances Tiafoe in Ohio.

Fils became the third Black man to win a Masters 1000 title, joining Ben Shelton, who won the Canadian Open twice, and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who won Paris in 2008 and Canada in 2014.

Tennis.summary: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula to meet in tournament's first all-American women's final in 56 years Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
The Cincinnati Open will host its first all-American women's final in 56 years after Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula won their respective semi-finals. Fourth seed Gauff cruised home in her clash with Sara Bejlek, eclipsing the Czech 6-4 6-1, while third seed Pegula earned her spot by toppling defending champion Iga Swiatek 7-5 4-6 6-4.

The last Cincinnati Open final to feature two American women came in 1970 when Rosie Casals defeated Nancy Richey. Fellow American Frances Tiafoe also reached the men's final, where he will face France's Arthur Fils.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu became a victim of her own success after her historic US Open triumph
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu became a victim of her own success after her historic US Open triumph Tennisuptodate.com
Tennis.body:
qualifying as a virtual unknown and walked out as a Grand Slam champion. It remains one of the most startling runs tennis has ever seen. Raducanu won 10 matches without dropping a set, becoming the first qualifier in history to win a Grand Slam singles title. What happened afterwards has been almost the opposite: five years of coaching changes, injuries and flashes of brilliance that have never quite turned into consistency.

That contrast makes Raducanu's career difficult to define. She isn't a simple story of wasted talent, because the talent still appears regularly. Nor is she simply an injury story, even though injuries have shaped almost every season since 2021. More than anything, Raducanu's career is a case study in how difficult it can be to build a career when the biggest result arrives before the foundations are ready to support it.

The withdrawal also marks the end of his planned mixed doubles run with Jessica Pegula, although the match-up was already uncertain as he had not received a wild card and in order to compete in the main draw he would have to go through the qualification rounds which run parallel with the mixed doubles event.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper ruled out of US Open
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper ruled out of US Open The Telegraph
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper has pulled out of the US Open after Jannik Sinner also withdrew from the final major of the year in a bitter blow to men’s tennis. Just weeks after he wept through an entire changeover – a moment Draper would later proclaim to be “rock bottom” – it appears there will be no immediate respite from a bone bruise in his elbow that has turned into a chronic problem.

Competing at the US Open was just too great an ask for a player who has already been beset by injuries but is one of the few on tour with the tools in his arsenal to threaten the top two.

Tennis.summary: “Doesn’t Get More Serious” – Injury Expert Explains Why Emma Raducanu’s Comeback Is Not Happening Anytime Soon Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
Injury expert Stephen Smith recently discussed Emma Raducanu's stress fracture and talked about the seriousness of the injury after the Brit withdrew from the U.S. Open. Raducanu is currently sidelined with a grade four stress fracture in her right shin. The injury initially started as a niggle during her run to the HSBC Championships final in June but quickly worsened, forcing her to withdraw from Wimbledon.

Following her Wimbledon withdrawal, Raducanu also pulled out of the U.S. Open after consulting with her medical team. The tournament is scheduled to take place from August 23 to September 13 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center.

Tennis.title: US Open offers biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history
Tennis.summary: The US Open will offer the biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history with a total of $108 million (£79.2m) on offer - marking a 20% increase on last year.
Tennis.body:
The US Open will offer the biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history with a total of $108 million (£79.2m) on offer - marking a 20% increase on last year. The singles' champions will receive $5.5m (£4.03m) each in a 10% increase on 2025.

First-round losers will take home $140,000 (£102,667) - which is $30,000 and 27% more than last year. The prize pool includes a $2m (£1.47m) contribution to a welfare fund, which leading players have been demanding from all the Grand Slams.

Tennis.title: One month or four years? Timing key in Kyrgios ban
Tennis.summary: The severity of the ban facing Nick Kyrgios for testing positive for cocaine depends on whether he can prove he took the drug out of competition.
Tennis.body:
The severity of the ban facing Nick Kyrgios for testing positive for cocaine depends on whether he can prove he took the drug out of competition. The 2022 Wimbledon finalist tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine at June's grass court event in Mallorca, and is currently serving a mandatory provisional suspension.

The ban could theoretically stretch to four years, but it will be a maximum of three months if the Australian can satisfy investigators he took the drug out of competition. A player is deemed to be 'in competition' from the day the draws they are competing in begin until they leave the tournament after their final match.

Tennis.title: 'I feel I am imprisoning myself'
Tennis.summary: Novak Djokovic discusses being his own biggest doubter and the Belgrade childhood that shaped him in a new documentary.
Tennis.body:
Nobody doubts Novak Djokovic more than himself. Djokovic has won almost everything there is in tennis. No man has more Grand Slam singles titles or Masters 1,000 crowns than him. He will go down in history as one of the greatest players of all time, if not the greatest.

But even now, at the age of 39, that is not enough for the Serb. "I cannot say I feel content with what I have and who I am," he says in a new Amazon documentary. "I am always looking to be more - better, faster, stronger. Oftentimes I feel I am imprisoning myself."

Tennis.title: Sabalenka stunned by Bejlek as slump continues
Tennis.summary: Aryna Sabalenka's preparations for her US Open title defence suffer a setback in a surprise defeat by Sara Bejlek at the Cincinnati Open.
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka's preparations for her US Open title defence suffered another blow as she crumbled in a surprise defeat by Sara Bejlek in the fourth round at the Cincinnati Open.

The Belarusian top seed was 5-1 up in a first-set tiebreak and 4-1 in front in the second set, but Czech Bejlek rallied back on both occasions to win 7-6 (9-7) 6-4. Sabalenka's position as world number one is now under threat, with Elena Rybakina - who faces Iga Swiatek in an eye-catching quarter-final on Thursday - able to replace her at the top of the rankings if she reaches the Cincinnati final.

Tennis.title: Why positive cocaine test could mean end of Kyrgios' career
Tennis.summary: Nick Kyrgios once said he did not want to play tennis into his 30s. A positive cocaine test could have brought an end to his career aged 31.
Tennis.body:
Nick Kyrgios once said there was "zero chance" he would be playing tennis into his 30s. But it was at the age of 31, while attempting another comeback from serious knee and wrist injuries, that he tested positive for a metabolite of cocaine at June's Mallorca Open.

Gauff won 68 per cent of her first service points in the match.

Golf.title: Gary Woodland's BMW Championship ended with an emotional (and meaningful) putt
Golf.summary: Gary Woodland's BMW Championship chances ended with a cold top, but his week still ended with an emotional and meaningful putt. The post Gary Woodland’s BMW Championship ended with an emotional (and meaningful) putt appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
All Gary Woodland could do was exhale and smile. It has been a trying few years for the 2019 U.S. Open champion, who underwent brain surgery in 2023 to remove a tumor and has been battling PTSD in the years since the operation. During an interview with Golf Channel in March, Woodland unburdened himself as he detailed how difficult it has been for him to compete on the PGA Tour while dealing with PTSD. Woodland said that going public with his diagnosis felt like lifting “1,000 pounds off his back.” Two weeks later, he won the Texas Children’s Houston Open to lift his first trophy since that Father’s Day in 2019 at Pebble Beach.

“Anybody that is struggling with something, I hope they see me and don’t give up,” a choked-up Woodland said moments after his final putt dropped in Houston. “It’s just another day, right, that I’ve got to keep healing. Today was a good day. But I’m going to keep fighting. I’ve got a big fight ahead of me and I’m going to keep going, but I’m proud of myself right now.”

Golf.title: Jon Rahm left facing uncertain future after LIV Golf season finale
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm left facing uncertain future after LIV Golf season finale The Independent
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm finished the LIV Golf season in style, claiming his third straight season points title and his second team crown in a row at the revised season finale in suburban Indianapolis. Now the 31-year-old Spaniard and the other full-time tour players will wait to see what happens to LIV in 2027.

Rahm is ready to head home and contemplate the future. “I’m looking forward to going home and helping my very pregnant wife with the kids,” Rahm said. “The fourth one is due in October, and I’m happy to be dad for a few days before I get back to grinding for the Irish Open, and mainly looking forward to a haircut because I need one badly.”

Golf.title: One in 322 billion
Golf.summary: Amateur golfer Allan Harrison - a former foursomes partner of Tommy Fleetwood - defies astronomical odds to card eight birdies across just nine holes.
Golf.body:
An ordinary round of golf turned into an extraordinary masterclass as an English amateur defied astronomical odds to card eight birdies across just nine holes. Allan Harrison started his round at Fairhaven Golf Club with four dropped shots down the front nine before a "pasty and a drink" at the halfway house gave him a burst of life.

The 64-year-old then fired seven consecutive birdies and eight in nine holes - a run of form rarely seen in professional golf, let alone at an amateur level. Harrison has some prowess as a former foursomes partner of Tommy Fleetwood at Southport and Ainsdale Golf Club.

Golf.title: Rising star Yamashita ties LPGA scoring record
Golf.summary: Rising star Miyu Yamashita ties an LPGA Tour scoring record as she surges to a dominant nine-shot victory at the CPKC Women's Open in Canada.
Golf.body:
Rising star Miyu Yamashita tied an LPGA Tour scoring record as she surged to a dominant nine-shot victory at the CPKC Women's Open in Canada. The 25-year-old from Japan made an eight-foot birdie putt on the 18th hole to complete a four-under 66 on Sunday and finish the week on a 23-under 257.

It matched Kim Sei-young 72-hole tour record lowest total, with the South Korean also carding 257 when finishing 31 under at Thornberry Creek in 2018. Yamashita broke the tournament's record of 262, set by South Korea's Ko Jin-young in 2019.

Golf.title: Is the music about to end? LIV Golf faces an uncertain future
Golf.summary: Is the music about to end? LIV Golf faces an uncertain future ESPN
Golf.body:
WESTFIELD, Ind. -- The music is stubborn and relentless, moving clumsily from rap to country to pop. At the Club at Chatham Hills, where the beat reverberates throughout the housing complex that surrounds the golf course with sameness, LIV Golf wants to convince everybody in attendance that they are guests at a party and not witnesses at a wake.

A smattering of fans sit on a small hill next to the par-3 12th tee box -- this week's "party hole," LIV's version of the 16th at the Phoenix WM Open -- sun-smacked and coated in layers of sweat. On the other side of the tee, a barricaded section labeled for holders of the "Grounds +" pass hosts no more than six people. The get-in price for the premium area was $81 at the beginning of the day, but by Thursday afternoon, it had been slashed to $53 just as Dustin Johnson stepped into the makeshift box and LIV's emcee tried his best to get the sparse crowd going.

Golf.title: The last days of LIV Golf and what the hell any of it was for
Golf.summary: The last days of LIV Golf and what the hell any of it was for Golf Digest
Golf.body:
Michael La Sasso’s final putt had barely disappeared before the champagne came out, his teammates dousing the former NCAA champion as he captured LIV Golf’s season finale in Indianapolis. The extravagance carried an uncomfortable dissonance, considering blue-collar workers were asking LIV to pay for labor already performed while millionaires emptied bottles over one another in celebration of additional millions. Still, LIV had reached a finish many doubted it would see, and La Sasso had earned his moment, even if this was almost certainly the last time anyone could spray champagne and pretend the league had a future worth toasting.

Because Sunday marked the end of LIV Golf as the sport had known it. An entity bearing the name may continue, with a schedule and teams and maybe a familiar face or two. But golf’s civil war is effectively over and what remains is worth accounting. What LIV ultimately represented and what it changed, whom it exposed and, after the billions spent and a sport fractured in two, what the hell any of this was actually for.

Golf.title: At the BMW, there was a cold top, mishits — and three Wyndham Clark bombs
Golf.summary: At the BMW Championship, there was a cold top, mishits — then three Wyndham Clark bombs at Bellerive Country Club. The post At the BMW, there was a cold top, mishits — and three Wyndham Clark bombs appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Wyndham Clark, leading by five strokes after the third round of the BMW Championship, was asked late Saturday afternoon what it would be like to go to sleep leading by five strokes after the third round of the BMW Championship, and he talked about the “angst when you wake up.” “You wake up,” Clark said, “and you have that little pit in your stomach.”

Fun, hey? Maybe for the folks in the gallery at Bellerive Country Club, or those watching from home. They saw pros having all kinds of un-fun during Sunday’s final round. There was Gary Woodland, who’s authored one of the best stories in recent memory by playing well this year while coping with the effects of having a brain lesion. He was a stroke out of the lead on the 9th hole — then bizarrely cold-topped a drive into the water about 100 yards in front of him on his way to a double bogey.

It has become tradition that the United States president contacts the winner at Trump International Golf Links in the immediate aftermath of their success. And Glaswegian Jamieson was the bewildered recipient of the call this time, following compatriot Grant Forrest last year.

Golf.title: Bizarre rules situation sees DP World Tour pro penalized … for divot kick
Golf.summary: A bizarre rules situation sees pro Shaun Norris penalized at the DP World Tour’s Nexo Championship for a divot kick. The post Bizarre rules situation sees DP World Tour pro penalized … for divot kick appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Shaun Norris’ right-foot strike, to Norris’ credit, looked pure. Unfortunately for him, he was playing golf, not soccer. The kick, along with the bizarre rules situation that followed, came during Sunday’s final round of the DP World Tour’s Nexo Championship, while Norris readied to play his second shot on the 382-yard, par-4 5th hole at Trump International Golf Links in Aberdeenshire, Scotland. There, while tied for the lead, Norris approached his ball in the fairway, then after a few seconds, took two steps backward.

That was a no-no under rule 8.1a (3) of the rules of golf, and about an hour later, Norris’ four on the hole was changed to a six. The rule addresses playing the course as you find it, and one action that is not allowed is “removing or pressing down divots that have already been replaced or other cut turf that is already in place.”

Varner is playing in LIV’s season-finale event at the Club at Chatham Hills outside of Indianapolis, but some social media posts alleged that Varner was part of a group that was kicked off one of the area’s top public courses, Bear Slide Golf Club, earlier in the week. Over the weekend Bear Slide posted its side of the story on its Facebook page, alleging that Varner booked a foursome, showed up 30 minutes late, and attempted to play as a sixsome.

“We accommodated the additional group and they were informed they could go off as 2 threesomes. At the first tee, they insisted that they should be allowed to play as a 6-some. The starter informed them again that is not allowed,” the post said. “After asking the starter 4 more times, one of the group members told the starter that he was being rude and needed to calm down. Another person from the group defended the starter, saying that he wasn’t being rude and was just enforcing the rules.

Golf.summary: LIV Golf should be a cautionary tale to other sports – but we won’t hold our breath The Irish Times
Golf.body:
Did you notice anything weird about the presentation ceremony at the World Cup final last month? Not the tragicomic sight of Gianni Infantino hustling Donald Trump offstage as Rodri and his Spanish team-mates lifted the trophy, as if Ol’ Burger Bite Face was a kind of incontinent grandpa who had wandered into a debs photo. That was weird, yes. But just the regular Trump kind of weird.

Wind the tape back a bit though, back as far as the presentation for Young Player of the Tournament to Pau Cubarsi, the 19-year-old Barcelona centre-back. The award has been on the go since the 2006 World Cup but there was something different about this go around. The camera panned to the right of the presentation party and there, in all his salt-and-pepper glory, stood Yasir Al-Rumayyan, ready to hand Cubarsi his bauble.

Golf.title: Good Good apologizes for controversial Callaway Golf video ad

Golf.body:
Good Good, a YouTube content outlet, apologized Saturday for a since-deleted video showing a man shoving a woman to the ground as part of an ad for a Callaway Golf golf club. “We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand,” the Good Good statement said. “We have since taken that content down. And sincerely apologize. Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward.”

A few hours later, a Callaway spokesperson shared the following statement with GOLF.com: “We are disappointed by the content that was posted, and are appreciative of Good Good for addressing this. We look forward to working together to ensure a more inclusive space in golf.”

Pros have used 5-woods for years, but now the 7-wood has become a viable option for high-speed players and even 9-woods have their fair share of users on the PGA Tour and around the world.

Golf.body:
Early extension is a swing flaw that afflicts many recreational golfers. When the pelvis shifts toward the ball too early during the downswing, you put yourself in a difficult position to make consistent contact. That’s why it’s crucial to correct the mistake when you see it infecting your swing.

Understanding the proper technique for eliminating early extension is important, but so too is teaching your body what it feels like to swing without it. That’s where utilizing a training aid comes in handy.

Golf.title: Is wrist movement ruining your putting stroke? Here's how to find out
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tom Stickney explains how your wrists should move during the putting stroke for optimal results. The post Is wrist movement ruining your putting stroke? Here’s how to find out appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The wrists are one of the most misunderstood elements of the putting stroke. Golfers are often told to keep the wrists quiet, but that does not mean they should be completely locked or rigid. The wrists are an important connection between the hands, arms and putter, and understanding their role can help create a more consistent stroke.

The first priority is understanding how the wrists influence the putter face. The lead wrist, or the wrist closest to the target, has a significant influence on how the face is delivered through impact. If the lead wrist changes dramatically during the stroke, the putter face can open or close, causing the ball to start away from the intended line. For that reason, a stable lead wrist is an important part of consistent face control.

Golf.title: Callaway's new Full Toe SP Wedges encourage creativity around the green
Golf.summary: Callaway's Full Toe SP wedges are aimed at increasing spin around the greens through the company's highest CG wedge yet. The post Callaway’s new Full Toe SP Wedges encourage creativity around the green appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Callaway‘s newest wedge was designed to solve a problem. When you open the face of a wedge, your strike tends to move toward the toe, where there aren’t always grooves, and farther from the CG.

The new Full SP Wedges solve this with a full-face groove design, giving you 44-percent more groove area than a conventional wedge, and a more optimized and higher CG to help you gain control around the greens.

Golf.title: Massive FedEx Cup bonuses get dished out Sunday at BMW Championship
Golf.summary: The PGA Tour's 2026 FedEx Cup bonuses are massive, and those payouts will be determined on Sunday after this week's BMW Championship. The post Massive FedEx Cup bonuses get dished out Sunday at BMW Championship appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
This week’s BMW Championship is the second-to-last event of the 2026 FedEx Cup playoffs, but it’s the final event to determine the season-long race for FedEx Cup bonuses. As part of rule changes made over last two seasons, the PGA Tour has decided to pay out the biggest FedEx Cup bonuses after the BMW Championship and before the season-ending Tour Championship.

And the payouts that will be distributed on Sunday are massive. The 2026 Tour Championship will still determine this year’s FedEx Cup champion, and the player who ends up on top at East Lake will earn $10 million.

Golf.title: Strained smiles and uncertainty
Golf.summary: BBC Sport visits LIV Golf's final event in its current guise to investigate what the future holds for the circuit that shook up the sport.
Golf.body:
It's been more than four years since the launch of LIV Golf rocked the game. A brash breakaway league, bankrolled by Saudi Arabian billions, luring top players with promises of big money.

Still it divides opinion in golf, and has split the loyalty of its champions. After the League's Saudi backers pulled its funding - having spent more than $5bn (£3.6bn) - this week's abortive season finale could be the end.

Golf.title: 'We have a lot against us': Bryson DeChambeau gets real about LIV's uncertain future
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau is still working to help LIV Golf survive, but on Thursday he conceded that those efforts may end up being unsuccessful. The post ‘We have a lot against us’: Bryson DeChambeau gets real about LIV’s uncertain future appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau is in the hunt at LIV Golf’s final tournament of the season following a strong first round. But the leaderboard may not have been the first thing on the two-time major champion’s mind on Thursday, nor anyone else’s.

While this week’s event, LIV Golf Indianapolis, wasn’t even supposed to be the last tournament of the year, it could end up being the final LIV Golf tournament ever played. The perilous situation LIV finds itself in was not lost on DeChambeau, the league’s biggest star, following his opening round in Indianapolis. Though he struck a few hopeful notes, DeChambeau also betrayed concerns about LIV’s uncertain future, and his own, in his comments.

Golf.title: Pre-order available now for TaylorMade's Hi-Toe 5 wedges
Golf.summary: The latest addition to the Hi-Toe family is now available for pre-order at Fairway Jockey: TaylorMade's Hi-Toe 5. Customize yours now! The post Pre-order available now for TaylorMade’s Hi-Toe 5 wedges appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you’re a confident chipper who prefers a full face of grooves on your wedge, chances are you’re a fan of TaylorMade’s Hi-Toe wedge family. These wedges are specifically designed to perform on open-face chips to give players maximum spin and versatility around the green.

Now, the latest addition to the Hi-Toe family is available for pre-order: TaylorMade’s Hi-Toe 5. These newly reimagined wedges are forged from soft carbon steel for the first time, and feature saw-milled grooves from top to bottom. Those all-important grooves are designed with ultra-tight tolerances, steeper walls and sharper radii to increase friction through impact.

Golf.title: The places golf can take you extend far beyond greens and grill rooms
Golf.summary: I wrote my first book, “The Green Road Home," 40 years ago. I didn’t know what I was doing, either as a caddie or writer, but I soaked it up. The post The places golf can take you extend far beyond greens and grill rooms appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I was 25 when I wrote “The Green Road Home,” in my parents’ house in Patchogue, on the South Shore of Long Island. On my 26th birthday a copy of it arrived there, hot off the press. That was in 1986. This piece is from a new afterword for it, a 40th anniversary edition that was published recently.

I was kind of amazed, the day that first copy showed up 40 years ago, as I didn’t know what I was doing, certainly not as a caddie, but not as a writer, either, not really. Since then, not much has changed. I’ve come to accept that as a writer and reporter my thing is to puzzle on through. For better or for worse, that’s my modus operandi, the swing thought of my professional life. Ask questions, look around, size things up, like a detective. (TV’s Lieutenant Columbo is one of my inspirations.) I don’t know what could be more fun than being a reporter.

Golf.title: McIlroy and Scheffler suffer reversal of fortunes
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy says a bit of "good work" with his team helped him rediscover his form and take the lead in the first round of the BMW Championship.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler had a reversal of fortunes that few could have predicted on Thursday's opening day of the BMW Championship in St Louis. Reigning Masters champion McIlroy, who finished 66th out of 70 at last week's St Jude Championship, was one of five players to post a six-under-par 64 at Bellerive Country Club to take the joint lead.

But world number one Scheffler, who last Sunday won the first of the PGA Tour's three no cut end-of season play-off events by eight shots, opened with a two-over-par 72. The American, who had only recorded an over par score once in his past 18 rounds, finished one shot above the worst score of the opening round and joint 44th in the 50-man field.

Golf.title: ‘Not become buffet meat’: LPGA pros are under attack by … mosquitoes
Golf.summary: The LPGA is playing the CPKC Women’s Open this week in Edmonton, Alberta, and the pros are under attack by mosquitoes. The post ‘Not become buffet meat’: LPGA pros are under attack by … mosquitoes appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Royal Mayfair Golf Club, by all accounts, deserves its first word — royal. There’s its history — it’s been around for 104 years. There’s its location — it’s in the heart of Edmonton, Alberta. There’s its golf — it’s tree-laden course has hosted men’s and women’s professional events, including this week’s LPGA stop, the CPKC Women’s Open.

Nelly Korda can certify its standing. The world’s top-ranked player said she’s found good coffee shops and restaurants. She said she’s been enjoying her time on the golf course. She’s also just been looking around. “The golf course is beautiful,” she said. “I mean, you kind of have the skyline of kind of downtown Edmonton, too, on the golf course, which is really pretty.”

Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tom Stickney shares six keys to focus on to perform better on the greens and reduce three-putts. The post 7 musts for becoming a better putter, according to a top teacher appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Putting can be mistakenly considered the simplest part of golf. The stroke is short, and there is no need to generate tremendous clubhead speed. Easy, right? As any avid golfer knows, that’s hardly the case. Although the stroke is small, putting is one of the most demanding skills in the game because small changes in alignment, balance, face angle or speed can produce dramatically different results. The margin for error is incredibly slim.

That’s why the key to becoming a better putter boils down to understanding a few fundamental principles and learning to repeat them under pressure. Check out below for a rundown of some of these key fundamentals and how they work together to create a solid stroke.

Golf.title: 'Definitely some players': Scottie Scheffler open to some LIV stars returning to PGA Tour

Golf.body:
As Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy are battling for big bucks at this week’s 2026 BMW Championship, LIV Golf’s season finale is going down in Indianapolis after the original finale was canceled. The upstart league’s future is in serious doubt, and some of its players are readying escape plans.

Whether or not LIV’s biggest remaining stars — like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm — will be allowed to return to the PGA Tour is an open question. McIlroy provided an unforgiving opinion on the matter during his Wednesday press conference ahead of the 2026 BMW Championship. McIlroy implied that the PGA Tour didn’t need LIV’s stars to come back. He did, though, admit that he expected them to return “eventually,” but that it would (and should) be a “tough, tough road back.”

Golf.title: 'If someone is willing to pay': Rory McIlroy defends skyrocketing prize money
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy, during his 2026 BMW Championship press conference, shot down the idea that there is too much money in pro golf. The post ‘If someone is willing to pay’: Rory McIlroy defends skyrocketing prize money appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy was on fire in his press conference ahead of the 2026 BMW Championship, even by normal Rory McIlroy standards. Never one to hide his true feelings from reporters, the World No. 2 continued that tradition at Bellerive Country Club on Wednesday.

First, he dumped cold water on the idea that returning LIV Golf stars could improve the PGA Tour, burning them with one line: “Have they brought value to LIV?” Then, he quieted any suggestion that he should win Player of the Year honors, handed Scottie Scheffler the title early and suggested that if Scheffler kept putting as well as he did last week, McIlroy and the rest of the Tour’s stars are “F’d.”

Golf.title: How a course's unusual act of kindness resulted in a teen caddie's $125,000 tip
Golf.summary: At 14, Daniella Penaloza lost her father and her love of golf. At 17, she caddied at Old Barnwell ... and earned a $125,000 tip. The post How a course’s unusual act of kindness resulted in a teen caddie’s $125,000 tip appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
LATER THIS WEEK, the students of greater Aiken, S.C., will return to school, and the weekday caddie yard at Old Barnwell will empty. Across enormous green fairways and inside bunkers shaped like dinosaur bones, it is usually not hard to find the teens of Aiken at Old Barnwell. They lumber around the golf course like percussionists in a folk rock band — their steps thumping against the hardened earth and their bags clanking with the sweet symphony of iron against iron.

Happen upon a game at Old Barnwell and you’ll quickly realize that it is not like other private golf clubs. Happen upon a conversation with one of Old Barnwell’s caddies and you’ll find out why.

Golf.title: 'Have they brought value to LIV?' Rory McIlroy questions PGA Tour returnees
Golf.summary: Should certain LIV Golf players be let back onto the PGA Tour? At the Tour’s BMW Championship, Rory McIlroy questioned their “value.” The post ‘Have they brought value to LIV?’ Rory McIlroy questions PGA Tour returnees appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy, when asked whether certain LIV Golf players should be allowed back onto the PGA Tour, started his 22-word answer on Wednesday with a question of his own. The six-time major winner spoke one day before the Tour’s BMW Championship — and at about the same time as LIV CEO Scott O’Neil addressed the future of his league as it attempts to regroup after the loss of its primary backer, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund. The exit has led to speculation on whether LIV players would stick with the league after its season-ending event this week, or look into avenues to play on the Tour, the circuit in which most of the pros had once played.

But McIlroy questioned the point of certain LIV pros returning. “I mean, I’d argue, have they brought value to LIV? You know?” he said. “I think the PGA Tour’s in a really good spot.”

Golf.title: Tiger Woods’ $120,999,166 record is about to fall. But it's not a fair fight
Golf.summary: Scottie Scheffler’s pursuit of Tiger Woods' career-earnings haul is a hot topic this week. But the chase needs to be kept in perspective. The post Tiger Woods’ $120,999,166 record is about to fall. But it’s not a fair fight appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When Scottie Scheffler tells you he’s a rich man, he’s not talking about his bank account. He’s referring to his family: high-school-sweetheart-turned-wife Meredith and their towheaded sons, Bennett (2) and Remy (5 months). He’s referring to his faith (he’s a devout Christian and regular at Park Cities Presbyterian Church in Dallas). And, in a distant third among his soul-fillers, he’s referring to his golf (though not in the name of chasing titles or history or fame; Scheffler is driven by the singular pursuit of executing each shot and each task as it comes — with as much care, skill and focus as his body and mind will allow).

None of which to say that the guy hasn’t also banked a Brink’s truck or two full of cash. Scheffler’s career windfall has come into focus this week as he prepares for the second of three legs of the PGA Tour’s FedEx Cup playoffs, the BMW Championship, because he is on the cusp of a seemingly momentous achievement: usurping Tiger Woods as the Tour’s all-time leading money earner. Scheffler ($119,964,411) trails Woods ($120,999,166) by “only” $1,034,755, meaning if he finishes in a three-way tie for third or better at Bellerive Country Club in St. Louis, Scheffler will assume the gilded throne. After Scheffler’s exemplary form in Memphis last week, where he won by a touchdown and a two-point conversion, smart money says Woods’ record will fall this week.

Golf.title: 8 things LIV’s CEO told reporters at season finale — and what they mean

Golf.body:
WESTFIELD, Ind. — For the second time in two weeks and perhaps the last time in quite a while, LIV CEO Scott O’Neil sat in front of cameras and reporters (and many interested LIV staffers) for a proper, professional press conference.

It lasted 33 minutes. It was nearly 4,000 words long. And there were some clues into LIV’s present and its future, among plenty of veiled coach-speak, CEO-speak, leader-speak. I’m here to parse through it on your behalf, like Trent Crimm of the Independent, aka the fictitious reporter from “Ted Lasso” — whom O’Neil himself likened me to during the proceedings.

Golf.title: 'Tough road back' to PGA Tour from LIV
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy feels it could be a "tough road back" to the PGA Tour for those players currently signed up to LIV Golf.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy feels it could be a "tough road back" to the PGA Tour for those currently with LIV Golf. After Saudi Arabia confirmed it was withdrawing financial backing to the breakaway league in April, uncertainty surrounding its future has increased with next week's Team Championship cancelled.

That has left this week's event in Indianapolis as LIV's season finale. In January, five-time Major winner Brooks Koepka rejoined the PGA Tour under a deal that saw him forfeit any player equity shares for the next five years, while he is also ineligible for the $100m (£73.4m) FedEx Cup bonus scheme this year and had to make a $5m (£3.6m) donation to charity.

Golf.title: Jack Whaley revisits the crucial shots from his U.S. Amateur win
Golf.summary: On this week's episode of Subpar, newly-minted U.S. Amateur champion Jack Whaley revisited the crucial shots from his winning week. The post Jack Whaley revisits the crucial shots from his U.S. Amateur win appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Like the U.S. Open, hopefuls must first qualify to gain entry into the tournament, either by their WAGR ranking or by going through local and final qualifying. Once there, 36 holes of stroke play determine which 64 of the 312 players in the field will move on to the match-play portion of the championship. This year, 16 players battled for the 11 remaining match-play spots at the end of the stroke-play portion of the championship.

Among those 11 players who got through was Jack Whaley, who became the newly-minted U.S. Amateur champion shortly thereafter. After punching his ticket to the Round of 64, Whaley had to defeat six consecutive opponents in order to claim the title.

Golf.body:
As a writer who traverses the globe covering golf, travel and all things food and beverage — and who racked up 110,000 frequent-flyer miles in 2025 — GOLF contributor Shaun Tolson has visited some of the world’s most famous golf clubs, resorts and best-kept secrets. Below, in Clubhouse Eats, he shares some of his favorite bites and sips from his recent travels.

It’s been more than 50 years since the advertising firm The Martin Agency (then Martin & Woltz Inc.) created the famous slogan “Virginia is for Lovers.” At the time, the slogan’s intention was to attract younger travelers to the state’s beaches, historical sites, and areas for outdoor adventure. But based on a few of my recent visits to Old Dominion — as the state is sometimes called — it’s clear Virginia is for food lovers, too.

Take it away, Rors.

Golf.title: Viktor Hovland's long odyssey is the product of what makes him great
Golf.summary: Viktor Hovland's search for the best version of himself is ongoing. It's the product of a double-edge sword that he must learn to manage. The post Viktor Hovland’s long odyssey is the product of what makes him great appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Viktor Hovland is curious. It has been both a blessing and a curse for the Norwegian star, and it’s what will eventually deliver him to what he has been searching for. Back in 2023, Viktor Hovland was one of the four best players in the world. He posted top 10s at the Players, the Masters and the PGA Championship before winning the Memorial, BMW and Tour Championship. It was the type of ascension Hovland had been destined to make ever since he turned pro in June of 2019. Everything pointed to Viktor Hovland continuing his rise, stacking wins and adding major championships to his resume. But Viktor Hovland is curious; he’s a dreamer and a wanderer and a tinkerer. So he decided to pick at his swing. Nitpicks became coaching changes and Viktor Hovland marched off on a path all his own making.

One he’s still trying to come back from. “Now, especially looking back, I would say that it was more I was content with my game up until — my whole career up until 2023 in terms of my ball striking,” Hovland said on Tuesday ahead of the 2026 BMW Championship. “But it was always trying to nitpick and trying to find places where I can improve. Now, with kind of the struggles that I’ve had the last, I would say, three years, where my ball striking has just been drastically worse, you know, you take a little bit for granted how good it was before.”

Golf.body:
European Ryder Cup legends Ian Poulter and Lee Westwood are set to make their returns to the DP World Tour (DPWT) later this year. The pair were among the first wave of players to be recruited by the LIV Golf League when it launched in June 2022.

Both golfers played in the opening tournament at Centurion Club and were subsequently hit with £100,000 fines for teeing it up without obtaining releases. They took the DPWT to a sports arbitration panel over the issue, but handed in their memberships after a panel of former high court judges ruled in favour of the Wentworth-based organisation in July 2023.

O'Neil announced two weeks ago that LIV Golf had secured an unnamed lead investor to keep the competition running in 2027 after the withdrawal of Saudi Arabian financial backing.

The former NBA executive said a signed agreement was in place and had been approved by LIV's board, with the transaction expected to be finalised next month. Golf.body:
LIV Golf’s season will end in Indianapolis this week – and the prize money payout for players has changed dramatically. LIV Golf has slashed expected payouts for the end of the creaking league’s season after the cancellation of the Team Championships in Michigan.

The final LIV event of the 2026 season will take place this week in Indianapolis, with the team finale now folded into the individual stroke play tournament at Chatham Hills. In normal regular individual events, LIV distributes $20million for its 57 players, with the winner banking a $4m cheque. But this week, the individual purse will be set at $10.1million, with the champion earning just over $2million. As was confirmed at the start of the season, the top three players in the individual standings will share a bonus of $10million.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau among players making contingency plans amid LIV Golf uncertainty
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau among players making contingency plans amid LIV Golf uncertainty The Japan Times
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau is among a number of players who have made commitments to tournaments on other tours following what could be LIV Golf’s final-ever event this week. The 2026 LIV Golf season will conclude in Indianapolis on Sunday. That was turned into the season-ending team championship after the event in suburban Detroit that was scheduled to take place from Aug. 27 to 30, was canceled with Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrawing its financial support following this season.

LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil is scheduled to hold a “League Update” news conference on Wednesday, with the league reportedly facing a Sept. 1 deadline to secure funding to continue in 2027.

Golf.title: 'I like pumpers': How Lee Trevino can tell if someone can ‘play’ golf
Golf.summary: Lee Trevino says he knows if a golfer can actually “play.” Here is one of his checks, which he talked about on a recently released podcast. The post ‘I like pumpers’: How Lee Trevino can tell if someone can ‘play’ golf appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
There are golfers, Lee Trevino says, who think they can “really” play golf. And some may be right. “There’s a bunch of them out there that think they can really play golf,” Trevino said. “When you’re an amateur, you’re an amateur. When you’re messing with the pros, you’re messing with the pros. It’s like boxing. You know, if you fought Golden Gloves, that’s everyone you ever fought, and now you’re going to fight a professional that’s been in the ring for 10 years, you’re going to get killed. Eventually, you’ll get killed.

“So it’s the same thing in golf. You might bite a little bit. You might get a crumb here and there every once in a while.” The question is, how can you tell if someone is a player — or a non-player? On a recent episode of the Vanity Index Podcast — which you can listen to in full here — the ever-popular Trevino said he has his methods.

Golf.title: Want to become a better ball striker? Start by improving these 4 things
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tony Ruggiero explains the four things he focuses on to help students hit the ball better without a swing overhaul. The post Want to become a better ball striker? Start by improving these 4 things appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I recently made it down to Key West, Fla., for a “working escape” with my good friend Wade Hamilton, the director of golf at Montgomery Country Club (and a great teacher in his own right). We spent an afternoon at Key West Golf Club with student Sam Steele, who was looking to make better contact with his irons. He wasn’t interested in a new golf swing, just in a way to find the center of the face more often so the ball would start doing what he wanted.

The good news is that he didn’t need a rebuild. He just needed four small adjustments to click into place, and once they did, Sam left with more than solid strikes. He left with an actual plan, which is usually the difference between a player who improves and one who just keeps hitting range balls at random. We worked through it with a handful of feels and drills built around those four fixes. You can see the whole session in the latest episode of our Pro Work series below.

Golf.title: My kids rejected golf. Would this backyard game have helped? | I tried it
Golf.summary: BucketGolf is a portable kit designed to make "golf a game that anyone can play." How well does it live up to that promise? The post My kids rejected golf. Would this backyard game have helped? | I tried it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
As a father who tried — and failed — to get his son and daughter into golf, I sometimes wander down What If Lane. What if we’d lived closer to a municipal course with a robust junior program? What if I’d joined a fancy country club that offered golf camps for kids? What if, instead of mobiles, I’d installed range finders in their cribs?

In short, was there anything I could have done differently to inspire my progeny to take up the game? The list of hypotheticals is long, and to it I will now add another: what if I’d introduced them to BucketGolf?

Golf.title: Production Company Sues LIV for $1.2M in Missed Payments
Golf.summary: Production Company Sues LIV for $1.2M in Missed Payments Front Office Sports
Golf.body:
As LIV Golf’s rocky 2026 season concludes this week, one of the league’s still-unresolved financial disputes dates back to before the season even began. Fresh Tape Media, the company that produced and operated the league’s preseason media days event in January, is suing LIV for more than $1.23 million in missed payments and interest, according to a complaint filed in the Supreme Court of the State of New York on July 21. Due to the nature of the lawsuit, LIV was formally notified of the complaint only on Monday—the same day it officially announced the cancellation of its $40 million team championship that was scheduled for next week in Michigan.

It’s the latest company to go public with claims of missed payments from LIV, as various vendors and contractors have told Front Office Sports they are also owed money by the league. Mobii Systems Group Limited, a former technology partner of LIV, also sued the league last month for more than $1.1 million for breach of contract, unpaid invoices, and interest.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: When measuring a club-length, is it legal to leave the headcover on?
Golf.summary: If you are measuring club-lengths for relief, is it permissible to keep your club's headcover on? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: When measuring a club-length, is it legal to leave the headcover on? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. During the Masters, Sam Burns took a penalty drop from Rae’s Creek. He measured two club-lengths from the agreed point of entry with his driver…but left the headcover on! He did the same playing with Matthew Fitzpatrick when Fitzpatrick won the U.S. Open. Is this legitimate? – Alan Absolon, via email

That depends — was the headcover a cute one? Like, in the shape of an animal, or with a pom-pom? We kid. As long as the ball ends up in the right spot, the Rules don’t really care how you measure. Unless a player is trying to use the extra length of the headcover and drops at the very end of the two club-lengths-plus-headcover, it doesn’t matter in the least whether the headcover stays on or not.

Rory McIlroy played the weekend at last week’s FedEx St. Jude Championship. But that’s only because the limited-field event didn’t feature a cut. The five-time major champion struggled through four rough rounds at TPC Southwind, eventually finishing third-to-last among the players who didn’t withdraw from the event.

Golf.title: Whaley earns Walker Cup spot after US Amateur win
Golf.summary: Jack Whaley is named in the 10‑man GB&I Walker Cup squad two days after winning the US Amateur Championship.
Golf.body:
Jack Whaley has been included in the Great Britain and Ireland team for the Walker Cup, two days after winning the US Amateur Championship. Whaley became just the third Englishman to lift the trophy since 1911 as he beat beat American Jay Leng Jr 4&3 in the final at Merion, Pennsylvania on Sunday.

The 22‑year‑old is one of four players included in the GB&I squad for the first time, alongside Ben Bolton, Sam Easterbrook and Josh Hill. Luke Poulter, son of Ryder Cup player Ian Poulter, is also in the 10-man squad for a second successive time after an impressive season with the University of Florida.

Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau has revealed he will be making a return to the DP World Tour this winter. The two-times US Open winner has not appeared on the circuit since 2022 and DeChambeau’s schedule for the 2027 season remains up in the air because of the ongoing uncertainty around LIV Golf.

DeChambeau has led the fight for LIV’s survival since it emerged the Saudi Public Investment Fund would be withdrawing its support at the end of the season. Ahead of his final LIV start of the season at Indianapolis, DeChambeau announced in a video with Gary Player that he would be teeing it up in this December’s Nedbank Golf Challenge. It will be DeChambeau’s second start in South Africa this year after he won on LIV’s inaugural visit in March.

Golf.body:
If sporting an athletic look is the on-course vibe that appeals most to you, Nike is likely a familiar brand in your closet. A decade after exiting the ball, club and bag side of the golf business, the Swoosh has remained synonymous with some of the game’s biggest names, partnering with World Nos. 1 and 2, Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy on the men’s side, and Nelly Korda and Michelle Wie West on the women’s side.

While we recreational players can’t necessarily ensure the same result as the pros when we try to replicate their equipment specs, we can certainly strive emulate their look as closely as possible by seeking out the apparel and footwear we see them wearing on Tour. And after Scheffler’s impressive performance at the FedEx St. Jude, we’re shining the spotlight on his Nike Victory Pro 4 spiked golf shoes, which you can buy at PGA TOUR Superstore.

Golf.title: Emotional Whaley credits dad for US Amateur glory
Golf.summary: It was very much a family affair for Jack Whaley as he became only the third Englishman to triumph in the US Amateur Championship on Sunday.
Golf.body:
It was very much a family affair for Jack Whaley as he became only the third Englishman to triumph in the US Amateur Championship on Sunday. The 22-year-old from Doncaster had his dad Andy caddying for him as he beat American Jay Leng Jr 4&3 in the final.

As a result, Whaley earned a place in the fields for the Masters, US Open and The Open at St Andrews in 2027, and an automatic berth in the Great Britain & Ireland Walker Cup team that will take on the United States at Lahinch in Ireland on 5 and 6 September.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Vendors Go Unpaid
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Vendors Go Unpaid Front Office Sports
Golf.body:
LIV Golf might be preparing for its next chapter with new investors, but more contractors and vendors claim they’re owed money by the league. The credit division of private investment firm BC Partners is exploring a funding deal with LIV to help the league continue operating in 2027 and beyond. This week’s LIV Golf Indianapolis event is set to pay out $30 million in prize money, and on Monday afternoon LIV Golf announced its season-ending $40 million team championship in Michigan next week is canceled.

As the tumultuous 2026 season comes to a close, no full-time employees are known to have seen any missed paychecks since the Saudi Public Investment Fund announced in April it would no longer fund LIV after this season.

Golf.body:
LIV Golf's season-ending Team Championship tournament in Michigan has been cancelled to allow "full resources" to be used to put plans in place for the 2027 calendar. Golf.title: LIV cancels final event to focus on 'next chapter'
Golf.summary: LIV Golf cancels its Team Championships in Michigan after weeks of speculation, saying it needs to focus on "building its next chapter".
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has cancelled its Team Championships in Michigan after weeks of speculation, saying it needs to focus on "building its next chapter". It had been widely expected that the event from 27 to 30 August would not happen, as players including Tyrrell Hatton entered the British Masters over the same dates and tickets were no longer being sold.

However, confirmation came on Monday with a statement from LIV Golf outlining changes to the schedule, meaning this week's event in Indianapolis will be the last of the season and double up as a team competition.

Badminton.title: French Scale Dizzy Heights
Badminton.summary: French Scale Dizzy Heights BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue and Alex Lanier helped France summit a peak that no European nation has done since 1977. Denmark won three gold at the inaugural year of the BWF World Championships; since then, no European nation achieved more than one gold at a single edition.

It was a historic day for France, with Gicquel/Delrue outplaying top seeds Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping in a tactical masterclass for the country’s first-ever gold, before Lanier imposed his physicality and speed on Kodai Naraoka to become the first French singles player to win the title.

Badminton.title: Alex Lanier scripts history, becomes first Frenchman to win BWF World Championships singles title
Badminton.summary: Alex Lanier scripts history, becomes first Frenchman to win BWF World Championships singles title The Times of India
Badminton.body:
, completing a remarkable run with a commanding straight-game victory over Japan's Kodai Naraoka on Sunday. The 21-year-old ninth seed produced a dominant display at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, beating 10th-seeded Naraoka 21-11, 21-11 in around 50 minutes to claim his maiden world title. Lanier controlled the match from the outset, combining aggressive attacking play with excellent court coverage to leave the Japanese shuttler struggling for answers.

The triumph caps a remarkable rise for Lanier, who had never previously reached a World Championships final. He had already made history by becoming the first Frenchman to reach the men's singles final at the event before taking the final step and becoming the country's first world champion in the discipline.

Badminton.title: Gicquel/Delrue: Golden Trailblazers
Badminton.summary: Gicquel/Delrue: Golden Trailblazers BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
France can celebrate their first-ever BWF World Championships gold after Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue outplayed top seeds Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping in a tactical masterclass: 22-20 19-21 21-15.

It is Europe’s first gold in a paired event since 2009 – incidentally, also in India — when Denmark’s Thomas Laybourn/Kamilla Rytter-Juhl won the title. The French completely took Huang out of the equation at the net, and even dared to flick-serve Feng from time to time. In fact, it was a flick serve on match point that finally delivered the historic moment for France.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships: French pair Gicquel and Delrue crowned world champions in mixed doubles
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships: French pair Gicquel and Delrue crowned world champions in mixed doubles WION
Badminton.body:
Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue have written a new chapter in French badminton history, defeating world no. 1 Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dong Ping in a thrilling three-set battle, 22-20, 19-21, 21-15. Partners for around a decade, the French duo produced one of the biggest wins of their careers against opponents who had beaten them in all four of their previous meetings. This time, however, Gicquel and Delrue controlled much of the contest and held their nerve when it mattered most.

The opening game was fiercely contested, with neither pair able to establish a significant advantage. After a superb rally finished by Gicquel gave the French pair their first game point, a Chinese mistake handed them the second opportunity they needed to take the opening set 22-20. Feng and Huang responded strongly in the second game. The Chinese pair raced into a 12-8 lead as the intensity increased, keeping the French duo at arm's length for much of the set. Gicquel and Delrue had an opportunity to draw level at 19-18 but could not take it, allowing their opponents to force a deciding game with a 21-19 victory.

Badminton.title: Gicquel/Delrue Break New Ground For France
Badminton.summary: Gicquel/Delrue Break New Ground For France BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
France can celebrate their first-ever BWF World Championships gold after Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue outplayed top seeds Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping in a tactical masterclass: 22-20 19-21 21-15.

It is Europe’s first gold in a paired event since 2009 – incidentally, also in India — when Denmark’s Thomas Laybourn/Kamilla Rytter-Juhl won the title. The French completely took Huang out of the equation at the net, and even dared to flick-serve Feng from time to time. In fact, it was a flick serve on match point that finally delivered the historic moment for France.

Badminton.body:
What a week New Delhi has given us. India waited 17 years for this moment, and India made every year count. The BWF World Championships 2026 have won praise from every corner of our sport. That praise belongs to the people, and I would like to name them.

The Badminton Association of India hosted these championships and held everything together over many months, from the first day to the last. The Government of India believed in this event. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports drove it forward. The Sports Authority of India delivered the arena.
