Badminton.title: Naraoka in History-Maker Lanier’s Path
Badminton.summary: Naraoka in History-Maker Lanier’s Path BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Alex Lanier followed his compatriots Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue in adding more chapters to the history books. After Gicquel/Delrue had become the first French to make a BWF World Championships final, Lanier authored his own subtext – becoming the first French player in a singles final. The journey to the final came through a hard test against Victor Lai, who too was in the reckoning to make history for Canada.

Lai dominated the early proceedings before Lanier’s endurance in the rallies changed the momentum. “At some point I was like ‘let’s fight, let’s play the rally’. I needed to trust that I’m consistent and stronger on court. That was the most difficult part of the match. The rallies were going long, I think it hurt me, but also Victor and definitely that was the momentum that I needed to catch,” said Lanier.

Badminton.title: Victor Lai Diary: The Campaign Ends
Badminton.summary: Victor Lai Diary: The Campaign Ends BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
A gruelling semifinal saw Alex Lanier leverage his physicality and outlast Victor Lai, stopping Lai from becoming the first Canadian in a BWF World Championships final. “The energy was a little low, but also, he was on the slower side so he could push me to the back and I had to worry about hitting it out, so he finished on the better side, which is always hard for me. I didn’t have a big enough lead in the end.

“I knew he’s physically probably the strongest player on the Tour, so he can always keep up his speed and his power for the whole three games. So that’s just kudos to him, and that’s something I need to work on.

Badminton.title: Gicquel/Delrue Make History for France
Badminton.summary: Gicquel/Delrue Make History for France BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
A first-ever final place for France at the BWF World Championships came with an unusual end-game. Having pulled level from a game down, Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue saw themselves steaming ahead of Jiang Zhen Bang/Wei Ya Xin with 12 points in a row. That phase effectively sealed the contest in favour of the French, for although the Chinese tried to make a match of it, the gap was too wide. Gicquel/Delrue bettered their performance from the last edition when they took home a bronze medal. This time it will be gold or silver against top seeds Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping.

“We were not ready to lead 12-0 in a semifinal,” said Delrue. “But we were really focussed on the first three shots and we put a lot of pressure on him (Jiang) specially. We wanted to show that nothing will be easy and at the end it was stressful because they played without pressure, so we needed to stay focussed after that.”

Badminton.summary: Top Seeds Survive Plucky Indonesians BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Amri Syahnawi and Nita Violina Marwah lifted themselves the way they never have, putting in performance of their lives to come within an inch of a final place at the BWF World Championships 2026.

It was the astonishing defensive abilities of Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dong Ping that stymied the Indonesians. Frequently defending from the floor and returning sure winners, the favourites earned their first title shot as a pair in a match that was decided by the narrowest of margins. The Chinese edged the Indonesians 20-22 21-14 22-20

Badminton.title: Chou Tien-chen secures 2nd BWF world championships medal with semifinal berth
Badminton.summary: Chou Tien-chen secures 2nd BWF world championships medal with semifinal berth Focus Taiwan
Badminton.body:
Taipei, Aug. 22 (CNA) Taiwanese badminton veteran Chou Tien-chen (周天成) advanced to the men's singles semifinals at the 2026 BWF World Championships in India on Friday, securing the second world championships medal of his career.

The 36-year-old world No. 6 defeated Indonesian rising star Alwi Farhan 21-15, 21-15 in 50 minutes to guarantee himself at least a bronze medal. Chou, who entered the match with a 2-1 career record against the world No. 12, used his defense and experience to neutralize Farhan's attacks and claim his third win in their four meetings.

Badminton.title: Denmark and France set for 2026 European Junior Team Championships final
Badminton.summary: Denmark and France set for 2026 European Junior Team Championships final Badminton Europe
Badminton.body:
The final is set in Tatabánya, with Denmark and France ready to battle for gold at the 2026 European Junior Team Championships. France booked their place by defeating Germany in the first semifinal. Germany put up a valiant effort, particularly in the second game, but France held firm to reach the final after finishing runners-up at the last three editions.

Defending champions Denmark had to dig deep against Türkiye. Türkiye led 53-50 late in the opening game, but Denmark fought back to take it 55-53. Türkiye continued their valiant effort throughout, before Denmark eventually secured a 2-1 victory.

Badminton.title: Victor Lai Diary: Medal Secured
Badminton.summary: Victor Lai Diary: Medal Secured BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
There are no extravagant celebrations backstage between Victor Lai and his team on securing a medal for the second time – just high-fives and a quiet word. It almost looked like they’d finished just any other match on the circuit.

But Lai knows better than to celebrate an unfinished campaign. Tomorrow he goes into the semifinals, the stage which he very nearly crossed last year. This time he’s a more complete player, more experienced, but with greater expectations on his shoulders.

Badminton.title: 'Battle against fear': Nozomi Okuhara reveals painful reason behind withdrawal from BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: 'Battle against fear': Nozomi Okuhara reveals painful reason behind withdrawal from BWF World Championships WION
Badminton.body:
Rio Olympics bronze medallist Nozomi Okuhara has revealed that she was forced to withdraw from her BWF World Championships quarterfinal against Pornpawee Chochuwong after pain from surgery she underwent last month became too difficult to manage. The 31-year-old Japanese shuttler had battled through a three-game match against USA’s Ishika Jaiswal in the previous round. The 57-minute contest appeared to have taken a physical toll on Okuhara, who was unable to continue in the quarterfinal.

Okuhara had already given a walkover to double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu in the quarterfinals of the Japan Open last month before undergoing surgery on July 22. Despite having just over a month to recover, she was determined to make it to the World Championships. “Since it was decided that I would undergo surgery on July 22, I have been aiming to step onto the court at this tournament," Okuhara tweeted on Friday morning.

Badminton.title: Nozomi Okuhara Withdraws From BWF World Championships 2026
Badminton.summary: Nozomi Okuhara Withdraws From BWF World Championships 2026 Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
Nozomi Okuhara has withdrawn from the BWF World Championships 2026 due to a knee injury, handing Pornpawee Chochuwong a quarterfinal walkover and a guaranteed medal. Japanese badminton star Nozomi Okuhara has taken a withdrawal from the BWF World Championships 2026. The reason behind the withdrawal is a knee injury. Nozomi was about to face Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong in the quarterfinals in New Delhi. After Nozomi’s withdrawal, the Thai player Pornpawee Chochuwong entered the semifinal directly. And she has guaranteed a medal in the tournament.

According to the latest , Okuhara, a former World No.1 player, entered the 2026 BWF World Championships with last success. She had won the women’s singles title in 2017. However, her campaign in BWF 2026 ended prematurely because of the injury. “I feel really happy to make a surprise for myself, especially yesterday because Chen is an Olympic gold medallist. This one big achievement is important for all athletes, we all want a medal in our career.” Said Chochuwong.

Badminton.title: Assured of Medal, Chochuwong Wrestles With Sadness
Badminton.summary: Assured of Medal, Chochuwong Wrestles With Sadness BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Pornpawee Chochuwong is no stranger to injury, and so she could empathise with the deep disappointment her opponent Nozomi Okuhara must have felt when the 2017 champion decided to withdraw from their quarterfinal due to a knee injury.

The withdrawal meant Chochuwong was guaranteed a World Championships medal – the biggest achievement of a long career marked by several injury layoffs. “I feel sad more than happy,” said the world No.10. “I understand her condition; injury is something you cannot control. I have also had a lot of injuries. I was sorry to hear that she was not well to play.”

Badminton.title: Shaunna Li Delivers Standout Performance for Oceania at BWF World Championships 2026
Badminton.summary: Shaunna Li Delivers Standout Performance for Oceania at BWF World Championships 2026 Badminton Oceania
Badminton.body:
Four Oceania players took to the court at the BWF World Badminton Championships 2026 in New Delhi, India. With a mix of experience and debut appearances, it was New Zealand’s Shaunna Li who delivered the standout result, fighting back from a first-game loss to win her opening match and book her place in the round of 32.

The tournament kicked off on 17 August, and while the rest of the Oceania contingent’s campaigns wrapped up in the early rounds, Li’s run continued a touch further. This year marked the first time the Oceania Women’s Singles Champion competed in both the women’s singles and the mixed doubles at a World Championships. For her, being surrounded by the best players in the world made for a memorable experience.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships 2026: ‘I don’t know if she was hurt or it was her strategy’: PV Sindhu after defeat to Wang Zhi Yi
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships 2026: ‘I don’t know if she was hurt or it was her strategy’: PV Sindhu after defeat to Wang Zhi Yi WION
Badminton.body:
PV Sindhu was left to rue a lack of patience in the closing stages after her BWF World Championships campaign ended with a defeat to China's Wang Zhi Yi. Sindhu, who was involved in a closely fought battle, felt the contest was largely under her control but admitted that she could have handled the crucial moments at the end better. “I think in the overall game, especially in the end, I should have been a little more patient,” Sindhu said after the match.

“I can't see any loopholes in between the points. I think in the end especially I should have been a little more patient. That's what I can see from today's game and in the last 3-4 points.” The former world champion was understandably disappointed with the result, particularly after being in contention for much of the match. “Yeah, disappointed of course. Sad about it, I should have converted that. But yeah, I mean that's how it is, that's how sport is,” Sindhu said. “You learn, you lose a lot, you win a lot. I mean when you lose you need to deal with it and bounce back stronger from your mistakes.”

Badminton.title: BWF banks on 15-point games to ease player workload
Badminton.summary: BWF banks on 15-point games to ease player workload Sportstar
Badminton.body:
The Badminton World Federation’s decision to introduce a 15-point scoring system from next season is driven primarily by concerns over player welfare and the increasing physical demands of the sport, Secretary General Thomas Lund said on Thursday. “It’s not a revolution, it’s an evolution of the scoring system,” he said.

Defending the change, he said matches had become longer and tighter as the depth of the sport had increased, meaning even the top players were facing significant physical demands from the opening rounds. “We’re now just tweaking the point system where the load on players will come down, so we actually safeguard the players and their health in a better way.”

Badminton.title: Victor Lai Diary: Déjà vu
Badminton.summary: Victor Lai Diary: Déjà vu BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
One year after he beat Loh Kean Yew at the BWF World Championships 2025, Victor Lai ran into the same opponent – this time in the Round of 16. Remarkably, when he came away after the 22-20 21-18 win, he knew it was the same score by which he had won last time.

Loh had almost run away with the first game with eight straight points, but Lai took it deep and nicked it. In the second he staged a mini-comeback with a display of immaculate control, defence, and opportunistic attack.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: Ayush Shetty Exits In Round Of 16, Faces Defeat To Indonesia 2-0
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: Ayush Shetty Exits In Round Of 16, Faces Defeat To Indonesia 2-0 Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
Ayush Shetty exits the men’s singles Round of 16 after losing to Indonesia 2-0 at the BWF World Championships 2026, held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi. The Indian badminton ace, Ayush Shetty, exited the BWF World Championships 2026 in the men’s Round of 16 after losing to the World No.11, Alwi Farhan, in two straight sets. In the latest sports news from Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, Ayush lost to the Indonesian shuttler with 19-21 and 11-21 in 45 minutes. The 21-year-old had a good run at the World Championships as he defeated the World No.1 in men’s singles.

Ayush Shetty came into the court with his two consecutive wins against the World No.1 Shi and Austria’s Filipino. The 21-year-old was cheered on by the crowd at the IG Stadium as he took charge against his opponent with three straight points. In the last meeting between the Indian shuttler and the World No. 11 in 2025, Ayush won 2-1. The game was level till 9-all, with Farhan throwing great smashes at Shetty. The Indonesian shuttler was quick with his strikes, hitting outstanding drop shots. The home player struggled to catch up in the latter half of the set, but he managed to end the set at 19 points. The opening set went to Farhan 21-19 in just 22 minutes.

Badminton.title: Chochuwong Stops Chen Yu Fei
Badminton.summary: Chochuwong Stops Chen Yu Fei BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Pornpawee Chochuwong shook off an unenviable record against Chen Yu Fei to take her place in the quarterfinals of the BWF World Championships 2026. It was a stubborn performance by the Thai, whose only win in 17 matches against the world No.4 had come eight years ago. Today Chochuwong dug in despite fluctuating fortunes in the second game, before staging a comeback from 6-13 in the third to clinch the match 15-21 25-23 21-17 in 84 minutes.

“I’m really happy to beat her because over the last few weeks I was injured at the Japan Open and China Open. I prepared well to play her and it worked,” said Chochuwong. “I just kept running and had to take every single shot she played, so I just had to be patient.

Badminton.title: 'We hope for players' understanding': BWF secy general Lund on India Open
Badminton.summary: 'We hope for players' understanding': BWF secy general Lund on India Open The New Indian Express
Badminton.body:
NEW DELHI: The India Open tournament has come under scathing criticism because of hazardous pollution in recent years. With player welfare in mind, the Badminton World Federation, while unveiling the 2027-2028 calendar earlier this year, had moved the event by a few weeks to February (2-7). However, that move was just made for the 2027 season and there are still concerns if that shift will bring about any major difference. BWF secretary general Thomas Lund said that they'll be examining all the data in the upcoming months and they are open to exploring all options in the future.

"There's obviously a lot of logistical things when you do these things and we have obviously been in close dialogue around it, the whole calendar and so coming into 2027, it's quite a short space. And for now, it hasn't been possible to totally move out of the first quarter. It is documented that pollution will go down a little bit further into January, February," Lund told reporters on the sidelines of the ongoing BWF World Championships in New Delhi.

Badminton.title: BWF: Synthetic shuttlecocks "inevitable" in badminton, but feathers won't disappear
Badminton.summary: BWF: Synthetic shuttlecocks "inevitable" in badminton, but feathers won't disappear sportstar.thehindu.com
Badminton.body:
The badminton shuttlecock may be on the verge of its biggest change in decades, but the feather is not about to disappear. BWF secretary general Thomas Lund says the federation expects synthetic-feather shuttlecocks to become an increasingly important part of badminton, including at higher levels of competition. But he stressed that the transition will be gradual and dependent on whether manufacturers can produce a shuttle that comes close enough to the performance of the best feather products.

“I think it’s inevitable that we move to a combination between the two,” Lund told Sportstar. “I’m not even sure that we’ll just move to just synthetic feather in years to come.”

Badminton.title: Garret Tan Sparkles on Great Day for Pan Am
Badminton.summary: Garret Tan Sparkles on Great Day for Pan Am BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
The BWF World Championships 2026 continued to throw up big-name casualties, with 14th seed Lakshya Sen falling to world No.92 Garret Tan on a great day for Pan Am. Tan, just 18, ranks No.7 on the World Junior rankings, but made light of the gulf in experience against the home favourite, as he dialled up his attacking game to leave Sen struggling throughout the match. Despite a nasty fall late in the third, Tan kept his composure to deal one of the upsets of the tournament and make his way into the Round of 16.

With compatriots Presley Smith/Jennie Gai and Ishika Jaiswal, and Canada’s Victor Lai and Michelle Li also winning their matches, Pan Am couldn’t have asked for a better day. “I can’t believe I won,” said Tan. “The last couple of tournaments I had the same problem, I was leading and I lost. I didn’t want to think about losing, I just wanted to focus.

Farhan, a former world youth champion, took victory in straight sets (21–12, 21–9) to progress to the third round - the last 16 stage of the men's singles competition. Badminton.title: Satwik-Chirag reach BWF Worlds pre-quarters without hitting a single shot: Here’s how
Badminton.summary: Satwik-Chirag reach BWF Worlds pre-quarters without hitting a single shot: Here’s how Open Magazine
Badminton.body:
Sometimes, at a World Championship, you need a perfect smash. Sometimes, you don't even need to pick up a racket. That was the rather unusual start to Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty's BWF World Championships campaign in New Delhi on Wednesday. The fifth-seeded Indians were scheduled to open their tournament against Scotland's Alexander Dunn and Adam Pringle.

Instead, the Scottish pair withdrew before the match. No rallies. No booming Satwik serves. No Chirag interceptions at the net. Just a walkover — and a place in the Round of 16.

Badminton.title: ‘I’ve Got You, Dad!’
Badminton.summary: ‘I’ve Got You, Dad!’ BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
A dream that Malvin Alcala had nurtured for himself over 40 years ago came to fruition when his son Mark Shelley took the court for his debut BWF World Championships. The senior Alcala was a promising player for the Philippines before a back injury in the early 1990s cut short his career and his dream of playing the World Championships and the Olympics. Everything he has done since then – naming his children, for instance, or moving to the USA later – was based around the ambition of seeing them achieve in badminton what he could not.

“This is my dream because it’s my dad’s dream,” said Alcala. “He got injured when he was a player, and he wasn’t able to achieve this dream. So he motivated me. Malvin Alcala was a late entrant to badminton. Raised in a family of modest means (his soldier father had died young), Alcala took up basketball and then stumbled upon badminton when he was 15. Having fallen in love with it and picking up its nuances through observation, he would start winning tournaments a year after he started.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: India’s Women’s Doubles Pair Wins Against USA In The Round of 32
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: India’s Women’s Doubles Pair Wins Against USA In The Round of 32 Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
The Indian women’s doubles pair of T Jolly and G Pullela claimed their consecutive win in the women’s Round of 32 at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, BWF World Championships, New Delhi 2026. The Indian duo defeated the United States’ L Lam and A Lee 2-0, with scores of 21-15 and 21-12 in just 39 minutes. In the latest sports news from the World Championships, Jolly and Pullela have advanced to the next round.

Indian pair started in a dominant position, taking control early in the game. They snatched the first set at 21-15 from the American pair in just 17 minutes. Jolly and Pullela looked in control in the second set as well, while the Americans struggled to find an opportunity, putting them on the back foot. The Indian shuttlers carried the momentum towards the blue corner, winning the second game 21-12 in mere 22 minutes.

Badminton.title: Turkiye Prevail in Humdinger
Badminton.summary: Turkiye Prevail in Humdinger BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
Two mixed doubles pairs who ply their wares on the fringes of the elite circuit produced the most intense match of the day at the BWF World Championships 2026. World No.71 Emre Sonmez/Yasemen Bektas and India’s Ashith Surya/Amrutha Pramuthesh (No.60), were locked in a 71-minute battle that see-sawed all the way before the Turkiye pair became the first from their country to make the second round. The Indians were in the reserves list and promoted to the main draw.

Sonmez and Bektas survived six match points in the second game to take it 30-29, and then saved two more in the third before converting their third opportunity: 16-21 30-29 24-22.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: The Mixed Doubles Pair Of R Kapoor And Gadde RS Exits In Round Of 64 After Losing To Canada 1-2
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026: The Mixed Doubles Pair Of R Kapoor And Gadde RS Exits In Round Of 64 After Losing To Canada 1-2 Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
The Indian mixed doubles pair of Rohan Kapoor and Ruthvika Shivani Gadde lost their first match against the Canadian pair of Jonathan Lai and Crystal Lai at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, BWF World Championships New Delhi 2026. In the latest sports news from the World Championships, Kapoor and Gadde lost to Canada 1-2 in a battle that lasted 1 hour and 8 minutes. They exited the BWF tournament with a score of 22-20, 19-21, and 17-21.

India’s mixed doubles pair of Rohan Kapoor and Ruthika Shivani started strongly, taking an early 3-point lead in the opening set. The Lai duo from Canada didn’t back down either, pushing the score in their favour. However, Kapoor and Gadde took 6 straight points, having the upper hand over the opponents. The Canadians made a comeback, taking the game to 11-14. The set got intense at 20-20, with both pairs fighting for the final point. The Indian pair won the battle at 22-20, taking the opening set at 1-0 in 20 minutes.

Badminton.title: Ratchanok beats Arin to reach BWF Worlds last 32
Badminton.summary: Ratchanok beats Arin to reach BWF Worlds last 32 Nation Thailand
Badminton.body:
Thailand’s Ratchanok Intanon made a convincing start to the BWF World Championships 2026 by defeating Turkey’s Neslihan Arin in straight games in New Delhi on Tuesday (August 18).

The former world champion won the women’s singles round-of-64 contest 21-14, 21-10 to book her place in the last 32. Ratchanok established control in the opening game before pulling further clear in the second, limiting Arin to 10 points as she closed out the match without dropping a game.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships 2026 Day 1 Highlights: India Makes Strong Winning Start I New Delhi
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships 2026 Day 1 Highlights: India Makes Strong Winning Start I New Delhi Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
BWF World Championships 2026 Day 1 highlights: India makes a strong winning start in New Delhi as Ayush Shetty, PV Sindhu and Indian doubles pairs shine. The BWF World Championships 2026 began with a banger for the Indian contingent. The opening day had several memorable performances. The impressive game was enjoyed by the fans across both singles and doubles. Ayush Shetty had the biggest victory by defeating world No. 1 and defending champion, Shi Yu Qi. While PV Sindhu also won the match. Meanwhile India’s doubles players delivered a mix of victories and competitive performances.

The biggest highlight of day 1 of badminton world championships came from Ayush Shetty. He stunned top seed Shi Yu Qi of China. Shetty won by 21-14, 13-21, 21-19 in 73 minutes. After taking the opening game, India lost the second but showed resilience and came out winning in the last round. PV Sindhu also added another convincing victory. She defeated Ireland’s S Noble by 21-7, 21-11. Together, the result of Ayush Shetty and PC Sindhu gave India’s single campaign an excellent start.
